Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by 10/15/20 % of its total Progression.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors repairing the Damaged Generator to scream.
This does not trigger a Loud Noise Notification.
Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance is disabled for the remainder of the Trial once all Tokens are consumed.
perks.name: Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance

killers.name: The Nightmare
killers.otzComment:
The Nightmare’s multiple abilities have great synergies with already strong perks and allow him to keep pressure on generators across any distance and sometimes cut chases short. While not particularly difficult to use mechanically, you will need to use all of your powers efficiently if you want to win against strong opponents.
Freddy has several abilities with different skill ceilings but he can still be enjoyed by players of any level. His perks are all endgame-oriented and are decent across the board. He'll become more powerful when you unlock gen-oriented perks such as Tinkerer and Pop Goes the Weasel.

teachables.name: Fire Up
teachables.desc:
The increased pressure of losing your preys fills you with anger and gives you unsuspected motivation.
For each completed Generator, Fire Up gains +1 Token, up to a maximum of 5 Tokens:
Increases the Action speeds for the following interactions by a stack-able 6/7/8 % per Token, up to a maximum of 30/35/40 %:
Picking up and dropping Survivors.
Breaking Breakable Walls and dropped Pallets.
Damaging Generators.
Vaulting Windows.

teachables.name: Remember Me
teachables.desc:
Whenever the Obsession loses a Health State by any means, Remember Me gains +1 Token, up to a maximum of 3/4/5 Tokens:
Increases the Opening time of both Exit Gates by a stack-able 6 seconds per Token, up to a maximum additional Opening time of 18/24/30 seconds.
This results in a maximum possible Opening time of 38/44/50 seconds for both Exit Gates.
Remember Me does not apply its penalty to the Obsession, allowing them to open both Exit Gates in the default time of 20 seconds.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.

teachables.name: Blood Warden
teachables.desc:
As soon as at least one Exit Gate is opened, Blood Warden activates:
The Auras of Survivors are revealed to you, whenever they are inside the Exit Gate.
Once per Trial, hooking a Survivor while Blood Warden is active calls upon The Entity to trigger the following effect:
Blocks all opened Exit Gates for 40/50/60 seconds, preventing any remaining Survivor from leaving the Trial through them.

builds.name: Generic Build
notes: Reliable and well-rounded build; a good starting point until you find the ideal build for your playstyle.

Your first three perks are the foundation of this build; damage gens around you when downing someone, reveal which gens are being worked on when you pick them up and quickly damage the gen after you teleport to it afterwards.
You could always switch out your 2nd and 3rd perk for ones that require you to actively kick the generator (such as Undone or Pop). This approach is a bit slower but hits gens even harder.
Your 4th perk is a flexible pick, but something that helps in chase could be appropriate!

perks.name: Thrilling Tremors
perks.desc:
After picking up a Survivor, Thrilling Tremors triggers its effects:
Blocks all Generators not currently being repaired by any Survivors for 16 seconds.
The Auras of Blocked Generators are highlighted to you in white.
Thrilling Tremors has a cool-down of 40/35/30 seconds.

alts.name: Tinkerer
alts.desc:
Whenever a Generator is repaired to 70 %, you benefit from the following effects:
Triggers a Loud Noise Notification for that Generator, revealing its location.
Grants the Undetectable Status Effect for the next 12/14/16 seconds.
Tinkerer can only trigger once per Generator per Trial.

perks.name: Turn Back the Clock
perks.desc: After hooking a Survivor, for 40/50/60 seconds, press the Active Ability button to make a target generator within 20 meters explode, lose -10 % progress, and start regressing.

perks.name: Surge
perks.desc:
Whenever you put a Survivor into the Dying State with your Basic Attack, Surge triggers its effect:
Causes all Generators within 32 metres of your location to instantly explode and start regressing.
Instantly regresses all affected Generators by 6/7/8 %.

alts.name: Undone
alts.desc:
For every time you hook a Survivor, Undone gains +1 Token, up to a maximum of 1/2/3 Token(s).
Performing the Damage Generator action on a Generator consumes all accumulated Tokens and applies the following effects:
Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by a stack-able -10 % of its total Progression per Token, up to a maximum of 10/20/30 %.
Blocks the Damaged Generator for 10 seconds per Token, up to a maximum of 10/20/30 seconds.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing once it becomes unblocked.

alts.name: Pop Goes the Weasel
alts.desc:
After hooking a Survivor, Pop Goes the Weasel activates for 35/40/45 seconds.
While active, manually damaging a Generator triggers the following effect:
Increases the regression amount by +15 % resulting in 20 % regression.
Pop Goes the Weasel deactivates after use or once its timer elapses.

perks.name: Coup de Grâce
perks.desc:
As the end nears, you go in for the kill.
Whenever a Generator is completed, Coup de Grâce gains +2 Tokens, up to a maximum of 10 Tokens per Trial:
Increases the range of your next Lunge Attack by 70/75/80 %, while consuming -1 Token.
Coup de Grâce can only hold a maximum of 5 Tokens at a time.

alts.name: Corrupt Intervention
alts.desc:
Your prayers invoke a dark power that meddles with the Survivors' chances of survival.
At the start of the Trial, the 3 Generators located farthest from you are blocked by The Entity for 80/100/120 seconds.
Corrupt Intervention deactivates prematurely once the first Survivor is put into the Dying State.

alts.name: Enduring
alts.desc:
You benefit from the following effect:
Reduces the duration of Pallet Stuns by 40/45/50 %.
This effect does not apply when stunned while carrying a Survivor.

alts.name: Ravenous
alts.desc:
Whenever you hook a Survivor for the first time, Ravenous gains +1 Token, up to a maximum of 4 Tokens.
For each Token:
Grants +4 % Haste Status Effect while carrying a Survivor.
Increases your hooking speed by +4 %.
Once you accumulate 4 Tokens, all Survivors suffer from the following effects:
Causes them to scream.
Inflicts the Exposed Status Effect for 80/85/90 seconds.

perks.name: Corrupt Intervention
perks.desc:
Your prayers invoke a dark power that meddles with the Survivors' chances of survival.
At the start of the Trial, the 3 Generators located farthest from you are blocked by The Entity for 80/100/120 seconds.
Corrupt Intervention deactivates prematurely once the first Survivor is put into the Dying State.

alts.name: No Holds Barred
alts.desc:
Each time a Generator is completed, No Holds Barred calls upon The Entity for the following effects:
Blocks the Generator with the most Progression for 15/20/25 seconds.
The Aura of the Blocked Generator is highlighted to you in white.

perks.name: Brutal Strength
perks.desc:
While performing the Break or Damage action on Breakable Walls, Pallets, or Generators, Brutal Strength triggers its effect:
Increases the Action speed by 10/15/20 %.

alts.name: Dragon's Grip
alts.desc:
After performing the Damage Generator action on a Generator, Dragon's Grip activates for 30 seconds.
While active, the first Survivor interacting with that Generator suffers from the following effects:
Causes them to scream and reveal their location for 4 seconds.
Inflicts the Exposed Status Effect for 60 seconds.
Dragon's Grip has a cool-down of 60/45/30 seconds.

perks.name: Fire Up
perks.desc:
The increased pressure of losing your preys fills you with anger and gives you unsuspected motivation.
For each completed Generator, Fire Up gains +1 Token, up to a maximum of 5 Tokens:
Increases the Action speeds for the following interactions by a stack-able 6/7/8 % per Token, up to a maximum of 30/35/40 %:
Picking up and dropping Survivors.
Breaking Breakable Walls and dropped Pallets.
Damaging Generators.
Vaulting Windows.

perks.name: Hex: No One Escapes Death
perks.desc:
Once the Exit Gates are powered, if there is still a Dull Totem remaining in the environment, Hex: No One Escapes Death activates and lights it:
Grants a 2/3/4 % Haste Status Effect.
Causes all Survivors to suffer from the Exposed Status Effect.
Once the Status Effect is revealed to Survivors, Hex: No One Escapes Death triggers the following effect:
The Aura of its Hex Totem is revealed to all Survivors within 4 metres.
This range gradually expands to 24 metres over the course of 30 seconds.
Hex: No One Escapes Death remains inactive if no Dull Totems are available.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

alts.name: Help Wanted
alts.desc:
After performing the Damage Generator action, Help Wanted activates:
Causes that Generator to become a Compromised Generator.
Up to 3 Generators can be Compromised at a time.
The Auras of all Compromised Generators are highlighted to you in yellow.
Once a Compromised Generator is completed, Help Wanted triggers its effects for 70/80/90 seconds:
Increases the Recovery speed of successful Basic Attacks by +25 %.
All Generators not being repaired will automatically regress at 150 % of the default Regression rate.
Additionally, all other Generators are no longer Compromised.

builds.name: Aggressive Scourge Build
notes: After hooking a Survivor on a Scourge Hook, the most progressed gen will be revealed (and possibly take damage). Teleport there and start your next chase quickly!
With "Rapid Brutality", you will be unexpectedly fast to catch to a Survivor after the initial hit. Feel free to switch it for another chase perk if you'd prefer.

perks.name: Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance
perks.desc:
Overwhelming pain reverberates outwards.
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Start the Trial with 4 Token.
Whenever a Survivor is hooked onto a Scourge Hook for the first time, Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance consumes -1 Token and applies the following effects:
Causes the Generator with the most progression to explode, damaging it.
Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by 10/15/20 % of its total Progression.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors repairing the Damaged Generator to scream.
This does not trigger a Loud Noise Notification.
Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance is disabled for the remainder of the Trial once all Tokens are consumed.

alts.name: Hex: Ruin
alts.desc:
All Generators not currently being repaired experience the following effect:
Causes them to automatically regress at 100/125/150 % of the default Regression rate.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

alts.name: Surge
alts.desc:
Whenever you put a Survivor into the Dying State with your Basic Attack, Surge triggers its effect:
Causes all Generators within 32 metres of your location to instantly explode and start regressing.
Instantly regresses all affected Generators by 6/7/8 %.

perks.name: Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine
perks.desc:
At the start of the Trial, the 4 Hooks located inside the Basement and an additional 4 Hooks located throughout the Trial Grounds are all changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of Scourge Hooks are highlighted to you in white.
Whenever you are farther than 24 metres from a Survivor hooked onto a Scourge Hook, the following effect applies:
All Generators regress at 150/175/200 % of the default Regression rate.

perks.name: Scourge Hook: Jagged Compass
perks.desc:
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Whenever a Survivor is unhooked from a normal Hook, the following effect applies:
The Hook is converted into a Scourge Hook.
Whenever you hook a Survivor onto a Scourge Hook, the following effect applies:
The Aura of the Generator with the most progression is highlighted in yellow for 6/8/10 seconds.

perks.name: Rapid Brutality
perks.desc:
You move with a speed and fury that makes blood run cold.
You can no longer gain the Bloodlust Status Effect.
Successfully hitting a Survivor with a Basic Attack grants you a +5 % Haste Status Effect for 8/9/10 seconds.

alts.name: Enduring
alts.desc:
You benefit from the following effect:
Reduces the duration of Pallet Stuns by 40/45/50 %.
This effect does not apply when stunned while carrying a Survivor.

alts.name: Bamboozle
alts.desc:
You benefit from the following permanent effect:
Increases your Vaulting speed by 5/10/15 %.
Whenever you vault a Window, Bamboozle calls upon The Entity for the following effect:
Blocks it to all Survivors for 8/12/16 seconds.
Vaulting it again within that time resets the timer.
Vaulting a different one transfers the effect to it instead.
Bamboozle does not extend its effects to vaulting a dropped Pallet.

builds.name: Beginner Perks Only
notes: Only uses perks available to this Killer or global perks available to everyone. It might include some alternative perk ideas from one of the five free Killers too.
Remember Me + NOED will make the endgame very volatile, especially if you manage to eliminate the Obsession ahead of time!
Sloppy Butcher is a decent source of slowdown, but you might want to replace it for some gen info perk to help you know where to teleport.

perks.name: No Holds Barred
perks.desc:
Each time a Generator is completed, No Holds Barred calls upon The Entity for the following effects:
Blocks the Generator with the most Progression for 15/20/25 seconds.
The Aura of the Blocked Generator is highlighted to you in white.

perks.name: Sloppy Butcher
perks.desc:
Survivors hit with your vicious Basic Attack suffer from the following effects for 70/80/90 seconds:
Inflicts the Haemorrhage and Mangled Status Effects.
Modifies the potency of Haemorrhage:
Increases the Spawn frequency of Pools of Blood by 50/75/100 %.
Increases the Regression rate of partial Healing progression by +25 %.

alts.name: Tinkerer
alts.desc:
Whenever a Generator is repaired to 70 %, you benefit from the following effects:
Triggers a Loud Noise Notification for that Generator, revealing its location.
Grants the Undetectable Status Effect for the next 12/14/16 seconds.
Tinkerer can only trigger once per Generator per Trial.

alts.name: Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine
alts.desc:
At the start of the Trial, the 4 Hooks located inside the Basement and an additional 4 Hooks located throughout the Trial Grounds are all changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of Scourge Hooks are highlighted to you in white.
Whenever you are farther than 24 metres from a Survivor hooked onto a Scourge Hook, the following effect applies:
All Generators regress at 150/175/200 % of the default Regression rate.

perks.name: Remember Me
perks.desc:
Whenever the Obsession loses a Health State by any means, Remember Me gains +1 Token, up to a maximum of 3/4/5 Tokens:
Increases the Opening time of both Exit Gates by a stack-able 6 seconds per Token, up to a maximum additional Opening time of 18/24/30 seconds.
This results in a maximum possible Opening time of 38/44/50 seconds for both Exit Gates.
Remember Me does not apply its penalty to the Obsession, allowing them to open both Exit Gates in the default time of 20 seconds.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.

alts.name: Unrelenting
alts.desc:
Basic Attacks benefit from the following effect:
Increases the recovery speed of missed basic-attacks by 30/35/40 %.
Increases the recovery speed of successful basic-attacks by 10 %.

perks.name: Hex: No One Escapes Death
perks.desc:
Once the Exit Gates are powered, if there is still a Dull Totem remaining in the environment, Hex: No One Escapes Death activates and lights it:
Grants a 2/3/4 % Haste Status Effect.
Causes all Survivors to suffer from the Exposed Status Effect.
Once the Status Effect is revealed to Survivors, Hex: No One Escapes Death triggers the following effect:
The Aura of its Hex Totem is revealed to all Survivors within 4 metres.
This range gradually expands to 24 metres over the course of 30 seconds.
Hex: No One Escapes Death remains inactive if no Dull Totems are available.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

addons.name: Jump Rope
addons.comment: Increases the already long movement penalty hinder applied by your snares. This makes them even more oppressive and hard to outplay in chase. The duration is so long that you can hit a Survivor with a snare right before a basic attack and they'll still be affected by the time their post-hit speed runs out. It's also one of the few ways to minimize the negative effect of Vigil, a perk that reduces the duration of this and other negative effects. A safe choice for any player.
addons.desc: Increases the duration of the -12 % Hindered Status Effect caused by Dream Snares by +0.5 seconds to 5 seconds.

addons.name: Pill Bottle
addons.comment: Makes the Survivors' sleep timer shorter each time they wake up, proggressively forcing them to waste time more frequently if they want to stay awake. This effect can become quite oppressive in prolonged matches.
addons.desc: Reduces the duration of the next instance of Microsleep for Survivors having entered the Dream World by falling asleep by a stack-able -10 %, up to a maximum of -50 %.

addons.name: "Z" Block
addons.comment: The aura reading from this add-on is very useful and triggers many times during a match, making it a very safe choice. Particularly useful when paired with the perk Lethal Pursuer, since it increases the aura read duration. Being able to see how Survivors move after being hit by a snare will eventually deepen your understanding of how they play against you, which makes this add-on an excellent training tool that will help you even when you eventually stop using it.
addons.desc: The Auras of Survivors affected by a Dream Snare or a Dream Pallet are revealed for 3 seconds.

addons.name: Nancy's Sketch
addons.comment: Reduces the immunity period that Survivors obtain after waking up from a clock, removing 6 seconds and bringing it down to 24 instead of 30 seconds. A really solid effect, since immune Survivors can be really challenging to chase. This effect is most noticeable when you're making the most out of the Nightmare's kit, teleporting often and switching targets constantly against a competent team that is trying to stay awake. Needless to say, if you focus on chasing the same Survivor for a long period of time and don't give them a chance to use a clock, this add-on will do nothing. It will also do nothing if Survivors don't make an effort to wake up frequently, but this is already a good scenario for you anyway.
addons.desc: Reduces the duration of Sleep Immunity by -20 %.

addons.name: Unicorn Block
addons.comment: Increases the range of the fake pallet's explosion by 0.5 meters when detonated by you. The larger radius makes it harder for Survivors to get away at the last second. The extra half meter makes a huge difference in several structures since it can allow the radius to envelop them fully and catch a Survivor that is looping them tightly. Even if you miss, the fact that a Survivor has to go further out of their way to dodge the explosion might make them easier to hit with a basic attack. Overall, this is a strong add-on with no downsides that will shine most in the hands of an experienced Nightmare player that can constantly micro-manage illusory pallet explosions.
addons.desc: Increases the Detonation radius of rupturing Dream Pallets by +0.5 metres.

addons.name: Class Photo
addons.comment: The ability to teleport to exit gates has great synergy with endgame builds but can also be used even earlier during the match in situations where an exit gate is located at a particularly useful spot to control an area or cut someone off. Pairs well with the iridescent Black Box.
addons.desc:
Grants the ability target the Exit Gate Switches with the Dream Projection ability.
Causes Survivors opening an Exit Gate to trigger Killer Instinct.

addons.name: Garden Rake
addons.comment: Increases the size of snares by 10%. Not extremely noticeable at first glance but a solid effect nonetheless, especially when you're trying to land snare hits on distant Survivors with unpredictable movement.
addons.desc: Increases the size of the Dream Snare by +10 %.

addons.name: Nancy's Masterpiece
addons.comment: Reduces the teleport cooldown by 10%, saving you about 3 seconds each time you hit a Survivor with a snare or fake pallet. This effect can be quite noticeable and result in much faster teleports, especially if multiple Survivors are hit in quick succession. However, having a shorter teleport cooldown isn't always extremely necessary, since you don't always need to use it right away anyway.
addons.desc: Reduces the Cool-down duration of Dream Projection by -10 % whenever a Survivor is struck by a Dream Ability.

addons.name: Outdoor Rope
addons.comment: Increases the speed of the dream snare projectile. More useful when hitting Survivors at a slight distance, but be careful not to rely too much on it since it might mess with your muscle memory when you take it off.
addons.desc: Increases the Travel speed of Dream Snares while placing them by +15 %.

addons.name: Prototype Claws
addons.comment: Increases the speed at which you can charge and release dream snares. Seems quite redundant, since the charge timer is so fast already, but being able to do it even faster does help make it feel more smooth during chase.
addons.desc: Reduces the Charge time of Dream Snares by -10 %.

addons.name: Black Box
addons.comment: When each exit gate is opened, this add-on traps any asleep Survivors for 15 seconds (and for a small extra 3 seconds if they wake up in any way). Highly situational, but this effect can catch Survivors off-guard and allow you to secure an extra kill at the endgame. Keep in mind that it can work once on each gate. If a Survivor is awake, you can put them to sleep with a basic attack or hit them from afar with a snare or two to prevent them from escaping at the last moment. Pairs well with endgame builds and the Class Photo for obvious reasons.
addons.desc:
Causes the Exit Gates to be blocked for Asleep Survivors for 15 seconds after they are opened.
This effect lingers for 3 seconds after those Survivors wake up.

addons.name: Green Dress
addons.comment: Slightly increases the duration of the wake up action that Survivors can perform on each other. Many Survivors will wake each other up before healing to avoid being teleported to, so this will delay them for a bit each time. This add-on is more valuable in lobbies without too many medkits where Survivors must rely on each other to heal. Not a bad effect at all, but remember that Survivors also have other ways to wake up that are not affected by this add-on.
addons.desc: Increases the time required to perform the Wake Up action by +2 seconds.

addons.name: Cat Block
addons.comment: Reduces the teleport cooldown by 10%, saving you about 3 seconds if you need to use it again. Not a terrible effect, but not extremely impactful either since you don't necessarily want to teleport right away anyway. Pretty useful if you're feeling lost and need to teleport to a different area of the map as soon as possible.
addons.desc: Reduces the Cool-down duration of the Dream Projection ability by -10 %.

addons.name: Wool Shirt
addons.comment: Reduces the delay of fake pallets when detonated remotely, giving Survivors less time to dodge or run past them. Pairs well with the blue Unicorn Block to make the pallets deadlier overall, but keep in mind that pallets can be quite hard to use early on in some maps and that it might be a risky idea to dedicate two add-ons to them. You can also try to make up for the lack of this add-on by triggering the explosion slightly sooner, if possible. Overall, this add-on's effect is nice but so small that it's sometimes hard to notice.
addons.desc: Reduces the Detonation delay of rupturing Dream Pallets by -10 %.

addons.name: Paint Thinner
addons.comment: Unlocks the ability to teleport to Survivors that drop a fake pallet at a faster rate than usual, and also reveals their location for a while with Killer Instinct. This is overall a very situational tool that might not even come into play a single time during the match. On top of that, Survivors that try to disrupt your fake pallets are probably not the ones you want to prioritize anyway. If you're gonna run it, try pairing it with the purple Swing Chains for a better chance to see value.
addons.desc:
Causes Survivors dropping a Dream Pallet to trigger Killer Instinct for 6 seconds.
Grants the ability to target these Survivors with the Dream Projection ability:
Increases the Charge speed of this Dream Projection by +100 %.

addons.name: Red Paint Brush
addons.comment: This add-on provides the extremely valuable ability to see distant Survivors who are asleep, giving you reliable information on their location. However, it comes at the huge cost of making their sleep timer 50% longer. This means they'll take 30 seconds longer to passively fall asleep and your snares will require one additional hit before putting them to sleep. Survivors being awake longer means they'll have an easier time healing without the fear of being teleported to. Overall, the tradeoff of this add-on is very negative and not worth the add-on slot unless you really know what you're doing.
addons.desc:
The Auras of Survivors trapped in the Dream World are revealed to you, whenever they are farther than 32 metres from your location.
Increases the default duration of Microsleep by +50 %.

addons.name: Kid's Drawing
addons.comment: Slightly increases the sleep timer "damage" of all of your abilities, making Survivors fall asleep sooner when hit by them. In some situations, this effect can occasionally save 3 or 6 seconds and allow you to immediately use a snare on a Survivor in chase. However, in most scenarios, Survivors will fall asleep after being hit with snares and this add-on will make basically no difference. Not a terrible effect for a brown add-on, but there are simply better ones.
addons.desc: Increases the amount of Microsleep gained from the Dream Abilities by +10 %.

addons.name: Sheep Block
addons.comment: Increases the time that a dream world clock is unavailable after being used, forcing Survivors to wait slightly longer before being able to use it again. Not terrible for an add-on of this rarity, but the effect is quite small. Don't forget that Survivors can also wake up in other ways.
addons.desc: Increases the Cool-down time of Alarm Clocks by +10 %.

addons.name: Swing Chains
addons.comment: This add-on blocks windows in a small 16 meter radius upon a successful teleport. Sadly, the effect is too brief and triggers way too late to be consistently useful. It can be paired with the Paint Thinner to possibly catch a Survivor by surprise who was trying to disrupt your fake pallets.
addons.desc: Blocks all Windows within 16 metres of your location for 6 seconds after using the Dream Projection ability.

addons.name: Blue Dress
addons.comment: This add-on reverts the snares back to their previous form before Freddy's rework. Instead of being a projectile, they become static circles. Not bad if you're feeling nostalgic, but overall a major downgrade compared to the default snares.
addons.desc:
Reduces the number of placeable Dream Snares to 1.
Causes the Dream Snare to be stationary while placing.
Causes the Dream Snare to automatically disappear after 8 seconds.

perks.desc:
You benefit from the following effect:
Reduces the duration of Pallet Stuns by 40/45/50 %.
This effect does not apply when stunned while carrying a Survivor.
perks.name: Enduring

perks.desc:
After hooking the Obsession, you benefit from the following effects for 14/16/18 seconds:
Grants the Undetectable Status Effect.
Grants a +10 % Haste Status Effect.
Whenever the Obsession is unhooked by another Survivor, the Obsession Status transfers to their Rescuer.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.
perks.name: Furtive Chase

perks.desc:
Whenever a Survivor other than your Obsession blinds you by any means or stuns you with a Pallet or a Locker, Nemesis triggers its primary effect:
Causes that Survivor to become your current Obsession.
Whenever your Obsession switches to a different Survivor by any means, Nemesis triggers its secondary effects:
Causes that Survivor to suffer from the Oblivious Status Effect for 40/50/60 seconds.
Their Aura is revealed to you for 8 seconds.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.
perks.name: Nemesis

perks.desc:
When you hook any Survivors that is not the Obsession, the following effects apply to the Obsession:
Their Aura is revealed for 6/8/10 seconds.
They suffer from the Exposed Status Effect for 20 seconds.
When you hook the Obsession, the following effects apply to a random Survivor:
Causes the Survivor to scream and reveal their location to the Killer.
They become the new Obsession.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.
perks.name: Friends ‘Til the End

perks.desc: Identical to Cull the Weak.
perks.name: Dying Light

perks.desc: Identical to Keep Them Waiting.
perks.name: Save the best for last

perks.desc:
You see your victim from afar and resolve to prolong their suffering.
After a Generator is completed, Hex: Wretched Fate activates and lights a random Dull Totem, cursing the Obsession:
Reduces their Repair speed by 27/30/33 %.
The Aura of the Hex Totem is revealed to them within 12 metres.
perks.name: Hex: Wretched Fate

perks.desc: Every 30 seconds, if the Obsession is 40 metres away from you, you see their aura for 2/2.5/3 seconds. Otherwise, the farthest Survivor becomes the Obsession.
perks.name: Celestial Witness

perks.desc:

This results in a maximum possible Opening time of 38/44/50 seconds for both Exit Gates.
Remember Me does not apply its penalty to the Obsession, allowing them to open both Exit Gates in the default time of 20 seconds.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.
perks.name: Remember Me

perks.desc:

Blocks both Exit Gate Switches for 12 seconds.
This time is extended by an additional 6/9/12 seconds per accumulated Token, up to a combined maximum of 36/48/60 seconds.

killers.name: The Pig
killers.otzComment:
The Pig doesn’t excel in any one area, but her several abilities (stealth, ambush, built-in slowdown…) can often be overwhelming for Survivors. Finding the correct synergy with your perks and add-ons is often the key to perform well.
The Pig is a fairly easy to play character with an invaluable ability to slow down the game with her power, which is particularly helpful for beginners. Her perks are not extremely powerful, although they often shine when paired together with other perks (such as Ruin + Surveilance).

addons.name: Jigsaw's Sketch
addons.comment: Having an extra reverse beartrap is an amazing effect by itself as long as you're getting enough downs to use all of them. With this add-on, you're even more likely to have at least one person trapped and unable to escape through exit gates during the endgame, which can allow you to bounce back from a difficult game. It can also be used to mitigate the downside of the iridescent Video Tape. The secondary effect of highlighting generators isn't always relevant, but it's nice to have still.
addons.desc:
Increases the number of carried Reverse Bear Traps by +1.
The Auras of Generators being repaired by Survivors wearing a Reverse Bear Traps are highlighted to you in yellow.

addons.name: Crate of Gears
addons.comment: Increasing the search time of Jigsaw boxes is an amazing effect that is guaranteed to give you reliable slowdown if you manage to use all of your reverse beartraps. The longer removal timer also means that it's easier for you to interrupt and reset them and that it's more likely that someone could actually die if their timer runs out.
addons.desc:
While attaching a Reverse Bear Trap to a downed Survivor, Crate of Gears applies its primary effect:
Increases your Action speed by +50 %.
Survivors searching a Jigsaw Box, Crate of Gears applies its secondary effect:
Reduces their Action speed by -25 %.

addons.name: Tampered Timer
addons.comment: Reduces the timer for active reverse traps, making it more likely that an unlucky Survivor might die to them. Since the amount of searches is not entirely random, this add-on can make it almost impossible for at least some Survivors to actually have enough time to remove their trap before they die. Not particularly strong by itself, but its effect is much more consistent when you also bring the purple Crate of Gears or if you are on a particular map that is difficult to navigate. Certain perks such as "Hex: Face the Darkness" can also randomly interrupt Survivors during searches to make them even longer. Keep in mind that this add-on will do literally nothing if your downs take too long and Survivors' traps aren't actually active for a long time.
addons.desc: Reduces the Death timer of Reverse Bear Traps by -20 seconds.

addons.name: Amanda's Secret
addons.comment: Reveals the location of a Survivor when they remove their reverse beartrap. With this add-on, you can often find vulnerable Survivors as soon as they start healing or right before they can work on generators again. A powerful effect, sadly limited by the Pig's own lack of mobility to fully take advange of it. Try to keep a mental image of where each trapped Survivor might be and you might have a better chance to hunt them down successfully.
addons.desc: Survivors removing their Reverse Bear Trap trigger a Loud Noise Notification and have their Auras revealed to you for 6 seconds.

addons.name: Video Tape
addons.comment: Places all of your reverse beartraps on the Survivors at the start of the game, typically making it so that every Survivor starts out trapped (unless you run Amanda's Letter). This effect is really powerful agaisnt uncoordinated teams (especially in maps that are difficult to navigate) and can buy you a lot of time at the start of the game. However, if you fail to capitalize on this early slowdown, you will find yourself in a really weak position where all Survivors have removed their traps and you no longer have anything to hold them back. Can be paired with the Annotated Plan or Jigsaw's Sketch to keep one more trap as a back up.
addons.desc: All Survivors start the Trial with a Reverse Bear Trap attached to them.

addons.name: Jigsaw's Annotated Plan
addons.comment: Having an extra reverse beartrap is an amazing effect by itself as long as you're getting enough downs to use all of them. With this add-on, you're even more likely to have at least one person trapped and unable to escape through exit gates during the endgame, which can allow you to bounce back from a difficult game. It can also be used to mitigate the downside of the iridescent Video Tape. The secondary effect is quite strange and actually visible for Survivors, since they get a debuff icon showing that a timer has been shortened. Most of the times, this secondary effect will do nothing (especially considering that it doesn't actually shorten the active timer if a generator is completed while the trapped Survivor is on the hook).
addons.desc:
Increases the number of carried Reverse Bear Traps by +1.
Increases the Death timer of Reverse Bear Traps by +10 seconds.
Reduces the Death timer of all Active Reverse Bear Traps by -10 seconds each time a Generator is completed.

addons.name: Bag of Gears
addons.comment: Increasing the search time of Jigsaw boxes is an amazing effect that is guaranteed to give you reliable slowdown if you manage to use all of your reverse beartraps. The longer removal timer also means that it's easier for you to interrupt and reset them and that it's more likely that someone could actually die if their timer runs out.
addons.desc:
While attaching a Reverse Bear Trap to a downed Survivor, Bag of Gears applies its primary effect:
Increases your Action speed by +50 %.
Survivors searching a Jigsaw Box, Bag of Gears applies its secondary effect:
Reduces their Action speed by -14 %.

addons.name: Workshop Grease
addons.comment: The increased charge speed is a really strong effect that makes the ambush easier to use. As explained for the Shattered Syringe add-on, the cooldown reduction effect is not very useful.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Ambush Dash attack with the following effects:
Increases its Charge speed by +50 %.

addons.name: Last Will
addons.comment: With the extra speed, your ambush covers more distance and is harder to react to. The downside of a longer charge can be mitigated by using the green Workshop Grease and doesn't always matter if a Survivor is already cornered. With these two add-ons combined, the Pig actually gains some distance on Survivors by the end of her ambush and can land hits that would otherwise be missed by a regular lunge attack. Overall, a pretty good effect.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Ambush Dash attack with the following effects:
Increases its Movement speed by +5 %.
Increases its Charge time by +10 %.

addons.name: Rules Set No.2
addons.comment: Removes the (normally visible) auras of the Jigsaw boxes until a Survivor's trap is active. This can be very disorienting for newer players or in indoor maps, where boxes are hard to find. Overall, this effect isn't all that powerful by itself since you typically do not want to encourage Survivors to repair generators instead of removing their trap. However, it can be quite useful when paired with the iridescent Video Tape (since everyone starts with a trap and the first generator won't be repaired for a while).
addons.desc: Disables the ability of Survivors to see the Auras of Jigsaw Boxes, until their Reverse Bear Trap becomes active.

addons.name: Combat Straps
addons.comment: Speeds up the animation of crouching and uncrouching. Somewhat noticeable in chase (especially if a Survivor keeps preemptively leaving the loop when they see you crouch), but the effect itself is quite small.
addons.desc: Increases the Transition speed into the Crouched State by +10 %.

addons.name: Face Mask
addons.comment: Applies the Blindness status effect to anyone wearing a reverse beartrap. A decevingly powerful effect, since it prevents Survivors from seeing all of their team mates while they're on the hook and also counters perks such as "Windows of Opportunity"  afterwards. Keep in mind that power-related props such as the Jigsaw boxes are still visible for blind Survivors, though.
addons.desc:
A modification to the Reverse Bear Trap:
The heavy cloth face mask, laced with a sedative, partially suffocates the target, making it hard to concentrate.
Survivors caught in a Reverse Bear Trap suffer permanently from the Blindness Status Effect.

addons.name: Amanda's Letter
addons.comment: Allows you to see Survivor auras near you at the cost of losing two of your beartraps. The aura reading effect is phenomenal and helps both in and out of chase (as long as Survivors don't have perks that hide their auras). However, the downside of losing half of your beartraps can be devastating in many cases, so one must use this add-on carefully.
addons.desc:
The Auras of Survivors within 16 metres are revealed to you when Crouched.
Reduces the number of carried Reverse Bear Traps by -2.

addons.name: John's Medical File
addons.comment: Slightly increases your movement speed when crouched. Even with this add-on, it's still generally not a good idea to crouch around the entire map looking for Survivors, as it's quite slow and inefficient. However, it pairs very well with information perks (so that you know where you're going) or aura reading from the iridescent Amanda's Letter. Some veteran Pig players might also be able to take advantage of this increased crouch speed to set up sneaky ambushes during chase.
addons.desc:
You benefit from the following effect:
Increases your Movement speed while Crouched by +5 %.

addons.name: Rusty Attachments
addons.comment: Applies the Mangled status effect to trapped Survivors. This can induce them into not healing after being unhooked or force them to waste a little bit of extra time, but it also has the potential to do nothing at all since it has a relatively short timer. Overall, this add-on is greatly outclassed by the Bag and Crate of Gears, since they provide a much more consistent form of slowdown that can actually make a much bigger difference.
addons.desc:
Survivors caught in a Reverse Bear Trap suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Mangled Status Effect for 70 seconds.

addons.name: Slow-Release Toxin
addons.comment: Applies the Exhaustion status effect to any trapped Survivor. Generally speaking, it's not a great idea to focus on chasing a trapped Survivor so making them exhausted is not extremely useful. Situationally useful, but definitely not a reliable choice.
addons.desc:
Survivors caught in a Reverse Bear Trap suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Exhausted Status Effect.

addons.name: Razor Wires
addons.comment: Much like its brown counterpart, this add-on is very unlikely to work in regular gameplay. However, it can be particularly useful when paired together with the Video Tape add-on. Since many Survivors will be frantically trying to remove their traps at the start of the game, the chances for one of them to be interrupted and take damage are much higher.
addons.desc:
A modification to the Reverse Bear Trap:
The addition of razor sharp wires makes it extra difficult and potentially painful to search them.
While healthy, Survivors failing a Skill Check at a Jigsaw Box become injured.
Increases the Skill Check difficulty by +20 %.

addons.name: Utility Blades
addons.comment: Applies the Haemorrhage status effect on Survivors with a reverse beartrap. This effect is simply too situational to be reliable. Trying to disrupt a trapped Survivor is often not ideal. Not to mention that some Survivors won't even try to heal if they're concerned about their timer running low.
addons.desc:
A modification to the Reverse Bear Trap:
Sharp blades attached to the Trap's interior lacerate the victim with every movement.
Survivors caught in a Reverse Bear Trap suffer from the Haemorrhage Status Effect whenever they are injured by any means.

addons.name: Interlocking Razor
addons.comment: Inflicting Deep Wound is a good effect, but the chances for this to trigger in a regular match are very, very low. There's not much you can do to actively make the skillchecks harder.
addons.desc:
A modification to the Reverse Bear Trap:
The addition of interlocking razor blades makes it impossible to move suddenly in the Jigsaw Box without slitting one's wrists.
While injured, Survivors failing a Skill Check at a Jigsaw Box become afflicted by the Deep Wound Status Effect.

addons.name: Shattered Syringe
addons.comment: The cooldown reduction effect is very small and does not actually work if you hit an obstacle. Hitting an obstacle is actually a good idea if you're about to miss an ambush as it has a shorter cooldown itself.
addons.desc: Reduces the Cool-down duration of missed Ambush Dash Attacks by -10 %.

killers.name: The Clown
killers.otzComment:
The Clown’s abilities are quite basic, but they can turn any greedy play by a Survivor into an almost guaranteed hit if they are applied correctly. With perks and add-ons to make up for his unremarkable mobility and lethality, the Clown can become a considerable threat.
 ---
The Clown's power is accessible to newer players and has an immense amount of depth for advanced players that learn to use both types of bottles in tandem. As a beginner, you might not want to play him immediately but you will definitely want to consider leveling him up for his amazing teachable perks. Pop Goes the Weasel is a solid gen regression perk and Bamboozle is an powerful chasing perk that's particularly useful on Killers with an instadown such as the Hillbilly.

alts.desc:
After hooking a Survivor, Pop Goes the Weasel activates for 35/40/45 seconds.
While active, manually damaging a Generator triggers the following effect:
Increases the regression amount by +15 % resulting in 20 % regression.
Pop Goes the Weasel deactivates after use or once its timer elapses.

perks.name: Scourge Hook: Weeping Wounds
perks.desc:
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Each time a Survivor is unhooked from a Scourge Hook, the following effects apply:
Causes that Survivor to suffer from the Haemorrhage Status Effect for 90 seconds.
After the first time that Survivor is healed back to full health, they suffer from the following effect until they are injured again by any means:
Reduces their Action speeds for Healing and Repairing by 10/13/16 %.

alts.name: Agitation
alts.desc:
While carrying a Survivor, Agitation activates:
Increases your Carrying speed by 14/16/18 %.
Increases your Terror Radius by +12 metres.

alts.name: Rapid Brutality
alts.desc:
You move with a speed and fury that makes blood run cold.
You can no longer gain the Bloodlust Status Effect.
Successfully hitting a Survivor with a Basic Attack grants you a +5 % Haste Status Effect for 8/9/10 seconds.

perks.name: Scourge Hook: Jagged Compass
perks.desc:
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Whenever a Survivor is unhooked from a normal Hook, the following effect applies:
The Hook is converted into a Scourge Hook.
Whenever you hook a Survivor onto a Scourge Hook, the following effect applies:
The Aura of the Generator with the most progression is highlighted in yellow for 6/8/10 seconds.

perks.name: Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance
perks.desc:
Overwhelming pain reverberates outwards.
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Start the Trial with 4 Token.
Whenever a Survivor is hooked onto a Scourge Hook for the first time, Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance consumes -1 Token and applies the following effects:
Causes the Generator with the most progression to explode, damaging it.
Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by 10/15/20 % of its total Progression.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors repairing the Damaged Generator to scream.
This does not trigger a Loud Noise Notification.
Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance is disabled for the remainder of the Trial once all Tokens are consumed.

alts.name: Dying Light
alts.desc: Identical to Cull the Weak.

alts.name: Discordance
alts.desc:
Any Generator within a range of 64/96/128 metres that is being repaired by 2 or more Survivors is marked by a yellow Aura.
When the Generator is first highlighted, Discordance triggers a Loud Noise Notification on the Generator.
After the Generator is no longer within range or is being repaired by just 1 Survivor, the highlighted Aura will linger for another 4 seconds.

perks.name: Surge
perks.desc:
Whenever you put a Survivor into the Dying State with your Basic Attack, Surge triggers its effect:
Causes all Generators within 32 metres of your location to instantly explode and start regressing.
Instantly regresses all affected Generators by 6/7/8 %.

alts.name: No Holds Barred
alts.desc:
Each time a Generator is completed, No Holds Barred calls upon The Entity for the following effects:
Blocks the Generator with the most Progression for 15/20/25 seconds.
The Aura of the Blocked Generator is highlighted to you in white.

alts.name: Hex: Ruin
alts.desc:
All Generators not currently being repaired experience the following effect:
Causes them to automatically regress at 100/125/150 % of the default Regression rate.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

builds.name: Beginner Perks Only
notes: Only uses perks available to this Killer or global perks available to everyone. It might include some alternative perk ideas from one of the five free Killers too.
A very aggressive build with tons of slowdown and endgame potential but little information. Feel free to swap in an information perk if you find yourself struggling to locate Survivors.

Pop Goes the Weasel allows you to damage gens even more than usual after performing a hook action. It has bad synergy with No Holds Barred since you can't kick a blocked gen, but they're still worth bringing together.

perks.name: Pop Goes the Weasel
perks.desc:
After hooking a Survivor, Pop Goes the Weasel activates for 35/40/45 seconds.
While active, manually damaging a Generator triggers the following effect:
Increases the regression amount by +15 % resulting in 20 % regression.
Pop Goes the Weasel deactivates after use or once its timer elapses.

perks.name: No Holds Barred
perks.desc:
Each time a Generator is completed, No Holds Barred calls upon The Entity for the following effects:
Blocks the Generator with the most Progression for 15/20/25 seconds.
The Aura of the Blocked Generator is highlighted to you in white.

perks.name: Sloppy Butcher
perks.desc:
Survivors hit with your vicious Basic Attack suffer from the following effects for 70/80/90 seconds:
Inflicts the Haemorrhage and Mangled Status Effects.
Modifies the potency of Haemorrhage:
Increases the Spawn frequency of Pools of Blood by 50/75/100 %.
Increases the Regression rate of partial Healing progression by +25 %.

alts.name: Tinkerer
alts.desc:
Whenever a Generator is repaired to 70 %, you benefit from the following effects:
Triggers a Loud Noise Notification for that Generator, revealing its location.
Grants the Undetectable Status Effect for the next 12/14/16 seconds.
Tinkerer can only trigger once per Generator per Trial.

alts.name: Spies from the Shadows
alts.desc:
Whenever a Survivor startles a Crow within 36/38/40 metres of your location, Spies from the Shadows triggers its effect:
Alerts you with a unique Loud Noise Notification in the shape of a Crow.
Spies from the Shadows has a cool-down of 3 seconds between alerts.

perks.name: Hex: No One Escapes Death
perks.desc:
Once the Exit Gates are powered, if there is still a Dull Totem remaining in the environment, Hex: No One Escapes Death activates and lights it:
Grants a 2/3/4 % Haste Status Effect.
Causes all Survivors to suffer from the Exposed Status Effect.
Once the Status Effect is revealed to Survivors, Hex: No One Escapes Death triggers the following effect:
The Aura of its Hex Totem is revealed to all Survivors within 4 metres.
This range gradually expands to 24 metres over the course of 30 seconds.
Hex: No One Escapes Death remains inactive if no Dull Totems are available.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

alts.name: Unrelenting
alts.desc:
Basic Attacks benefit from the following effect:
Increases the recovery speed of missed basic-attacks by 30/35/40 %.
Increases the recovery speed of successful basic-attacks by 10 %.

addons.name: Cheap Gin Bottle
addons.comment: Increases your speed by 3% when invigorated by yellow bottles. Particularly useful when used by experienced players that use both types of bottles effectively during chase. Pairs well with the blue Flask of Bleach.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Antidote with the following effect:
Increases the strength of the Haste Status Effect by +3 % to +17 %.

addons.name: Garish Make-Up Kit
addons.comment: Increases the duration of the yellow bottle's speed boost. It can be stacked with its green counterpart. If used with the Cigar Box, it also extends the time during which you can see auras. It's a strong effect if you're using yellow bottles often.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Antidote with the following effect:
Increases the duration of Invigoration by +2 seconds.

addons.name: Ether 15 Vol%
addons.comment: Increases the lingering effect of the slowdown bottles by 0.5 seconds which is an additional 50%. A really strong and straight-forward effect.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Tonic with the following effect:
Increases the duration of Intoxication by +0.5 seconds.

addons.name: Sticky Soda Bottle
addons.comment: Increases your speed by 2% when invigorated by yellow bottles. Particularly useful when used by experienced players that use both types of bottles effectively during chase. Pairs well with the blue Flask of Bleach.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Antidote with the following effect:
Increases the strength of the Haste Status Effect by +2 % to +16 %.

addons.name: Thick Cork Stopper
addons.comment: Slightly increases the reload speed. Particularly useful if you use a yellow bottle at your feet right before reloading, as it can make the reloading process even smoother and make you lose minimal distance against a Survivor running away from you. Arguably more useful than its blue counterpart, although you can combine both of them if you want to have super fast reloads.
addons.desc:
You benefit from the following effect:
Reduces the Reloading time by -0.5 seconds.

addons.name: Tattoo's Middle Finger
addons.comment: A very simple add-on that shows the aura of Survivors affected by your bottles. Very easy to use and the aura reading is almost always helpful in one way or another, even if it's just to inform you that a Survivor managed to utilize one of your yellow gas clouds against you.
addons.desc:
Survivors afflicted by the Tonic or the Antidote suffer from the following effect:
Their Auras are revealed to you for 6 seconds.

addons.name: Solvent Jug
addons.comment: Increases the duration of the already decent yellow bottle speed boost. It can be stacked with its purple counterpart.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Antidote with the following effect:
Increases the duration of Invigoration by +1 second.

addons.name: Cigar Box
addons.comment: Turns your yellow bottles into information-gathering tools that can help you to keep track of Survivors during chase and sometimes even outside of it, if you're lucky enough. It has quite a limited range, however.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Antidote with the following effect:
The Auras of all Players within 6 metres are revealed to the Invigorated Players for 6 seconds.

addons.name: Sulphuric Acid Vial
addons.comment: Applies a decently useful status effect, but applying it to multiple Survivors at once is very difficult on a Killer with such a limited mobility.
addons.desc:
Survivors afflicted by the Tonic suffer from the following effect:
Causes the Mangled Status Effect for 70 seconds.

addons.name: Smelly Inner Soles
addons.comment: Greatly increases your movement speed during reload, making the process a lot smoother overall. The effects are very noticeable if you made a mistake and must reload while you're chasing after a Survivor. If you're reloading at a loop while the Survivor is stuck with you, this add-on will basically do nothing.
addons.desc:
While replenishing your Bottles, you benefit from the following effect:
Increases your Movement speed by +15 %.

addons.name: Starling Feather
addons.comment: Reduces the bottle toss cooldown significantly, allowing you to spam bottle throws or perform an attack sooner, for example. Can be stacked with its brown counterpart, although there's not much reason to do so.
addons.desc:
You benefit from the following effect:
Reduces the Cool-down time after throwing a Bottle by -50 %.

addons.name: Robin Feather
addons.comment: Reduces the bottle toss cooldown significantly, allowing you to spam bottle throws or perform an attack sooner, for example. It's almost as strong as its green counterpart.
addons.desc:
You benefit from the following effect:
Reduces the Cool-down time after throwing a Bottle by -40 %.

addons.name: Flask of Bleach
addons.comment: Slightly increases the hinder effect from your slowdown bottles. This can sometimes make a difference in loops (where Survivors are forced to go through the entire gas cloud) or if you're running the purple Ether 15 Vol% to increase the lingering duration. However, in most situations, the 2% increase is simply not worth the add-on slot over other options.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Tonic with the following effect:
Increases the strength of the Hindered Status Effect by -2 % to -16 %.

addons.name: Fingerless Parade Gloves
addons.comment: This add-on sharply changes the throw angle of the bottles, making them follow a more straight path similar to Huntress hatchets instead of their normal curved arc. Generally speaking, this throw angle is completely unnecessary and will often hurt your ability to learn Clown as a beginner. It also makes throwing bottles over some obstacles much harder. However, despite these clear downsides, this add-on does have some unique advantages. Its secondary effect of increasing the throw speed by +25% is very helpful to hit Survivors in some situations where a regular throw would be too slow. The faster speed also means that bottles can travel further, allowing you to throw them at distant targets more easily. Advanced players might get some value from this add-on if they learn its unique quirks, but new players would do well to stay away from it.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Bottles with the following effects:
Increases their Throw speed by #effect(1).
Reduces their Throw angle by #effect(2).

addons.name: Kerosene Can
addons.comment: This add-on provides an easy way to apply blindness, but it typically comes too late in chase to have any real utility. The duration is also very short, which means it won't do much afterwards.
addons.desc:
Survivors afflicted by the Tonic suffer from the following effect:
Causes the Blindness Status Effect for 30 seconds.

addons.name: Bottle of Chloroform
addons.comment: This add-on increases the size of the slowdown gas clouds and also makes them spread out slightly faster indirectly. This makes it even harder for Survivors to avoid them in some cases, but the situations where this effect makes a real difference are pretty rare. In a worst case scenario, it can even help Survivors by spreading the gas clouds too far apart and creating gaps between them. If you want to enhance your slowdown bottles, the Ether 15 Vol% is a much better choice.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Tonic with the following effect:
Increases the size and spread of the Gas Clouds by +20 %.

addons.name: VHS Porn
addons.comment: This add-on increases the size of the slowdown gas clouds and also makes them spread out slightly faster indirectly. This makes it even harder for Survivors to avoid them in some cases, but the situations where this effect makes a real difference are pretty rare. In a worst case scenario, it can even help Survivors by spreading the gas clouds too far apart and creating gaps between them. If you want to enhance your slowdown bottles, the Ether 15 Vol% is a much better choice.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Tonic with the following effect:
Increases the size and spread of the Gas Clouds by +10 %.

addons.name: Party Bottle
addons.comment: This add-on has no effect and since the confetti is visible to Survivors, they will become immediately aware that you wasted an add-on slot. If you need the extra bloodpoints, don't worry about it though.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Tonic and Antidote with the following effects:
Bottles now release confetti upon breaking, in addition to their usual effects.
Direct hits with a Bottle grant 100 bonus Bloodpoints in the Deviousness Scoring Category.

addons.name: Spirit of Hartshorn
addons.comment: Increasing the size of yellow clouds is not particularly useful. At best, it can help to make sure that you don't accidentally walk past it and miss out on the effects. At worst, it could spill out too far and end up on the wrong side of a loop which could benefit Survivors. Definitely not worth running compared to other add-ons of its rarity.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Antidote with the following effect:
Increases the size and spread of Gas Clouds by +20 %.

addons.name: Redhead's Pinkie Finger
addons.comment: This add-on provides a strong insta-down (if you can successfully land a direct hit with your bottle) but comes at the huge cost of limiting your maximum capacity to a single bottle. This greatly diminishes the versatility of your bottles and is typically not worth running over other add-ons unless you really know what you're doing. You might want to pair this with the green Thick Cork Stopper to at least reload faster after each bottle toss.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Tonic with the following effect:
Survivors hit directly with its Bottle suffer from the Exposed Status Effect while Intoxicated.
Redhead's Pinkie Finger limits the number of carried Bottles to 1.

Undetectable Status Effect

killers.name: The Spirit
killers.otzComment:
The sheer unpredictability of the Spirit’s power puts a lot of power into your hands while simultaneously making it extremely difficult for Survivors to make the right decisions in chase. Her chasing potential is off the charts once you get used to the intricacies of her phasing.
The Spirit has one of the most unique powers in the roster that requires you to deduce Survivor locations without actually being able to see them. She plays very differently from almost any other Killer and will be difficult for most beginners to grasp. That being said, her perks are fairly simple to use and a decent choice to unlock for newer players.

teachables.name: Spirit Fury
teachables.desc:
After manually breaking a total of 4/3/2  dropped Pallets by any means, Spirit Fury activates:
Instantly breaks the next Pallet used by a Survivor to stun you.
Spirit Fury deactivates after use and does not affect the duration of the Pallet Stun.

teachables.name: Hex: Haunted Ground
teachables.desc:
Hex: Haunted Ground lights 2 Hex Totems at the start of the Trial, laying a trap for Survivors.
Blessing or cleansing either Hex Totem trips the trap and triggers the following effect:
Causes all Survivors to suffer from the Exposed Status Effect for 40/50/60 seconds.
Hex: Haunted Ground extinguishes the second Hex Totem after tripping its trap.
Hex: Haunted Ground is disabled for the remainder of the Trial after triggering its effect.

teachables.name: Rancor
teachables.desc:
Whenever a Generator is completed, Rancor triggers its primary effects:
Causes all Survivors to scream and trigger a Loud Noise Notification at their current location.
This effect lingers for 3 seconds.
Your Aura is revealed to the Obsession for 5/4/3 seconds.
Once the Exit Gates are powered, Rancor additionally triggers its secondary effects on the Obsession:
Inflicts the Exposed Status Effect for the remainder of the Trial.
Grants the ability to kill them when in close proximity.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.

builds.name: Generic Build
notes: Reliable and well-rounded build; a good starting point until you find the ideal build for your playstyle.
Focuses extremely heavy on slowdown. If you don't need the info from your 4th perk, you could slap another slowdown perk on top of this already stacked build for massive regression.

perks.name: Corrupt Intervention
perks.desc:
Your prayers invoke a dark power that meddles with the Survivors' chances of survival.
At the start of the Trial, the 3 Generators located farthest from you are blocked by The Entity for 80/100/120 seconds.
Corrupt Intervention deactivates prematurely once the first Survivor is put into the Dying State.

Highlights its Aura to you in yellow.
Triggers a Loud Noise Notification whenever a Survivor succeeds a Good Skill Check while repairing it.

perks.name: Barbecue & Chilli
perks.desc:
A deep bond with The Entity unlocks potential in one's Aura-reading ability.
After hooking a Survivor, all Survivors who are at least 60/50/40 metres away from that Hook have their Aura revealed to you for 5 seconds.

alts.name: Nowhere to Hide
alts.desc:
Performing the Damage Generator action on a Generator triggers Nowhere to Hide:
The Auras of all Survivors within 24 metres of the Generator's location are revealed to you for 3/4/5 seconds.

alts.name: Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance
alts.desc:
Overwhelming pain reverberates outwards.
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Start the Trial with 4 Token.
Whenever a Survivor is hooked onto a Scourge Hook for the first time, Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance consumes -1 Token and applies the following effects:
Causes the Generator with the most progression to explode, damaging it.
Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by 10/15/20 % of its total Progression.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors repairing the Damaged Generator to scream.
This does not trigger a Loud Noise Notification.
Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance is disabled for the remainder of the Trial once all Tokens are consumed.

perks.name: Starstruck
perks.desc:
Whenever you are carrying a Survivor, Starstruck activates:
Causes all other Survivors in your Terror Radius to suffer from the Exposed Status Effect.
This effect lingers for 26/28/30 seconds after affected Survivors leave the Terror Radius or Starstruck deactivates.
Starstruck deactivates after hooking or dropping the carried Survivor and has a cool-down of 60 seconds.

alts.name: Ravenous
alts.desc:
Whenever you hook a Survivor for the first time, Ravenous gains +1 Token, up to a maximum of 4 Tokens.
For each Token:
Grants +4 % Haste Status Effect while carrying a Survivor.
Increases your hooking speed by +4 %.
Once you accumulate 4 Tokens, all Survivors suffer from the following effects:
Causes them to scream.
Inflicts the Exposed Status Effect for 80/85/90 seconds.

perks.name: Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance
perks.desc:
Overwhelming pain reverberates outwards.
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.

Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by 10/15/20 % of its total Progression.
