addons.name: Jump Rope
addons.comment: This add-on increases the maximum reach of all of your dashes, which can allow you to hit Survivors that would otherwise be slightly too far away. It also helps a bit when using your power for mobility. It's a modest effect but still quite reliable and can often make the difference between a miss and a hit.
addons.desc: Extends the duration of Slice & Dice to 108 % of its default duration.

addons.name: Power Drill
addons.comment: Slightly reduces your power recovery after a successful special attack. Being able to use your power again sooner is almost always useful to help end chases sooner, even if it's only a little.
addons.desc: Reduces the Cool-down duration of Hidey-Ho Mode by -10 % after successful Slice & Dice Attacks.

addons.name: Straight Razor
addons.comment: Good and simple effect. The status effect only lasts 80 seconds but that should be plenty for most scenarios.
addons.desc: Survivors hit with successful Slice & Dice Attacks suffer from the Haemorrhage and Mangled Status Effects for 80 seconds.

addons.name: Yardstick
addons.comment: The aura read can sometimes reveal hidden Survivors and make it easier to track the ones that you're after. It doesn't always come into play, but the effect is quite decent still, especially if you're adept at chaining his scamper to occasionally cover large distances quickly. Pairs well with other scamper-related add-ons.
addons.desc: Performing a Scamper reveals the Auras of all Survivors within 16 metres of you for 3 seconds.

addons.name: Iridescent Amulet
addons.comment: Has a small downside but makes your power last much longer. Since going into stealth mode makes Survivors see illusory footprints, you don't necessarily want to always be using your power if you don't know where you're going. This add-on pairs best with information perks so that you can approach undetected and keep every Survivor on the map guessing where you might be. It's definitely at its strongest when playing against newer Survivors or on indoor maps where even experienced Survivors don't have much visibility.
addons.desc:
Extends the duration of Hidey-Ho Mode by +50 %.
Basic Attacks immediately end Hidey-Ho Mode.

addons.name: Rat Poison
addons.comment: This add-on reveals Survivors during you dash attack. Critically, the aura remains for a bit of time after the hit, which often allows you to perfectly track Survivors and avoid losing them when out of line of sight. The initial aura reveal also makes it even easier to land your special attacks in some scenarios. Particularly useful when paired with the perk Lethal Pursuer to enhance its lingering effect.
addons.desc:
While performing a Slice & Dice attack, benefit from the following effect:
The Auras of all Survivors within 6 metres of your location are revealed to you for 2.5 seconds.

addons.name: Hair Spray & Candle
addons.comment: This add-on reduces the amount of power gauge that you lose if you use a basic attack on a Survivor. This can sometimes allow you to retain enough power to be able to follow up a basic attack with a special dash attack, which could easily happen if a healthy Survivor comes to take a hit to protect a vulnerable teammate. Even if it only triggers a few times per match, it can still be quite decent.
addons.desc: Reduces the Power-Gauge penalty of Basic Attacks when in Hidey-Ho Mode by -20 %.

addons.name: Portable TV
addons.comment: Only works during endgame, but the effect is ridiculously strong. You can catch up to Survivors very quickly or cut them off before they reach an exit gate. Keep in mind that if you perform a long dash and then vault a window or pallet, you will get another long rush immediately after.
addons.desc: Extends the duration of Slice & Dice to 170 % of its default duration once the Exit Gates have been powered.

addons.name: Running Shoes
addons.comment: This add-on provides a small 2% haste speed boost after a scamper, but since you're not able to transition into normal movement afterwards, this boost is not particularly usable in small loops. However, this increased speed does allow you to reach further and possibly even chain multiple scampers together to cover large distances quickly. Chaining multiple scampers also makes the 2% boost stack on top of itself briefly, possibly giving you 4% or 6% for a brief moment, which can make your miss cooldown feel a bit less punishing. If you want to have a longer dash consistently even without scamper, using the green Jump Rope is probably a better idea, although you can also pair them together. Don't bother running this add-on if you're not confident in your ability to scamper correctly and consistently.
addons.desc: Performing a Scamper grants a +2 % Haste Status Effect for 5 seconds.

addons.name: Automatic Screwdriver
addons.comment: Allows you to recover slightly faster and use your power again sooner after a missed attack. The effect is rather small and doesn't help if you are accurate with your special attacks, but it's still fairly decent otherwise.
addons.desc: Reduces the Cool-down duration of Hidey-Ho Mode by -8 % after missing a Slice & Dice Attack.

addons.name: Hard Hat
addons.comment: This add-on allows you to break a pallet when you scamper underneath it. This does not have a downside itself, but scampering under pallets during chase isn't always the best idea since you have very little control of where your dash can go afterwards. Keep in mind that Chucky used to be able to scamper pallets without starting a Slice & Dice dash, but then this ability was taken out of his kit at one point. This add-on is best used to clean up dropped pallets after a chase has ended and while you're chaining scampers together to traverse the map.
addons.desc: Instantly breaksPallets, when performing a Scamper under them.

addons.name: Strobing Light
addons.comment: The reduction of terror radius is already nice on its own, but it can shine even further when paired with other things that also reduce your terror radius.
addons.desc: Reduces your Terror Radius by -8 metres, when Hidey-Ho Mode is on cool-down.

addons.name: Silk Pillow
addons.comment: This add-on has a signficant downside and should never be used carelessly. However, it can be somewhat decent when paired with other add-ons and perks that reduce your terror radius. You will need some information gathering perks to make the most of this reduced terror radius, but it can definitely work out sometimes.
addons.desc:
Permanently reduces your Terror Radius by -6 metres.
Increases the Charge time of Slice & Dice to 150 % of its default duration.

addons.name: Good Guy Box
addons.comment: Reducing your cooldown is always a good thing, but this add-on has a very tiny effect that is almost unnoticeable and doesn't typically make much of a difference in chase.
addons.desc: Reduces the Cool-down duration of successful Slice & Dice Attacks to 93 % of their default duration.

addons.name: Electric Carving Knife
addons.comment: Reducing your cooldown is always a good thing, but this add-on has a very tiny effect that is almost unnoticeable and doesn't typically make much of a difference in chase.
addons.desc: Reduces the Cool-down duration of missed Slice & Dice Attacks to 95 % of their default duration.

addons.name: Doll Eyes
addons.comment: You should generally only use your power when you're already chasing a Survivor, so the information from this add-on isn't always super relevant. Still, not too bad.
addons.desc: When in Hidey-Ho Mode, the Auras of all Windows and downed Pallets are revealed to you within 20 metres.

addons.name: Pile of Nails
addons.comment: Ending your power manually is something that happens very rarely during normal gameplay, but with this add-on you can do it on purpose to catch Survivors off-guard with an extra Undetectable status effect. Perceptive Survivors will typically notice the illusory footprints and when they disappear, so they'll assume that you're far away somewhere else, making them less likely to run away early. However, the extremely limited duration of 3 seconds and your below average mobility makes this strategy almost impossible to consistently pull off. It's best paired with perks such as Discordance that will maximize your chance to actually catch one or more Survivors off-guard when you remain Undetectable for those 3 seconds.
addons.desc: Grants the Undetectable Status Effect for 3 seconds after manually ending Hidey-Ho Mode.

addons.name: Plastic Bag
addons.comment: This add-on can sometimes cause Exhaustion to random Survivors across the map, but the effects are highly inconsistent, especially if you use your power in short bursts (which you should). On top of that, it's basically impossible to tell if a Survivor has been affected by this add-on. Needless to say, if Survivors don't have any exhaustion perks, this add-on is also completely useless.
addons.desc: Survivors walking through an Illusory Footfall suffer from the Exhausted Status Effect for 15 seconds.

addons.name: Tiny Scalpel
addons.comment: You should generally only use your power when you're already chasing a Survivor, so the small tracking advantage that this add-on provides is almost useless.
addons.desc: When in Hidey-Ho Mode, Pools of Blood appear to you in bright red.

addons.name: Mirror Shards
addons.comment: The tracking that this add-on provides is incredibly inconsistent and situational. Generally speaking, you do not want to go into stealth mode if you don't already know where Survivors are. On top of that, it also makes the illusory footsteps audible, which results in their sounds getting mixed together with the real sounds from Survivor footsteps and overall making tracking harder. Don't run this unless you know what you're doing.
addons.desc: Grants the ability to see the Illusory Footfalls around Survivors.

killers.name: The Unknown
killers.otzComment:
The Unknown is an incredibly unpredictable Killer capable of leaving behind clones that he can teleport to later, which can be used for mobility or even in chase. He also possesses an explosive projectile attack capable of damaging multiple Survivors, even through obstacles. Great precision and awareness are required to make the most out of his powers.
Since the Unknown's special attack inflict a status effect that can be dispelled by staring at him, beginner players might find it difficult to learn him for a while. However, his perks are generally very strong and can be used by almost everyone in the Killer roster. Undone and Unforeseen are the two that stand out the most for their ability to damage generators and keep you stealthy.

teachables.desc:

Vaulting a Window while Unbound is active grants a +5 % Haste Status Effect for 25 seconds.
This effect cannot stack with itself.

Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing once it becomes unblocked.

Grants the Undetectable Status Effect.
Unforeseen has a cool-down of 30 seconds.

builds.name: Ambush Build
notes: Hyper-aggressive build popularized by u/Relhtar. It revolves around constant hit and run and never committing to unproductive chases. You never chase in the open where Survivors can dispel UVX status easily.
Kicking gens sets them up for future damage (Eruption) and turns you undetectable (Unforeseen), making it more likely to find healing Survivors with Nurse's Calling.
Works best with double iridescent add-ons!

perks.name: A Nurse's Calling
perks.desc:
Unlocks potential in your Aura-reading ability:
The Auras of Survivors being healed or healing themselves are revealed to you within 28/30/32 metres.

alts.name: Nowhere to Hide
alts.desc:
Performing the Damage Generator action on a Generator triggers Nowhere to Hide:
The Auras of all Survivors within 24 metres of the Generator's location are revealed to you for 3/4/5 seconds.

perks.name: Eruption
perks.desc:
Performing the Damage Generator action on Generators highlights their Auras in yellow.
Whenever a Survivor enters the Dying State by any means, Eruption triggers the following effects on all highlighted Generators:
Causes them to explode, damaging them.
Instantly regresses them by -10 % of their total Progression.
Causes them to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors currently repairing them to suffer from the following effects:
Causes them to scream.
Their Auras are revealed to you for 8/10/12 seconds.
Eruption has a cool-down of 30 seconds after triggering its effects, which also resets the highlighted Auras.

perks.name: Unforeseen
perks.desc:
After performing the Damage Generator action on a Generator, you benefit from the following effects for 22/26/30 seconds:
Transfers your Terror Radius to the damaged Generator.
This Terror Radius is set to 32 metres.
Grants the Undetectable Status Effect.
Unforeseen has a cool-down of 30 seconds.

perks.name: Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance
perks.desc:
Overwhelming pain reverberates outwards.
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Start the Trial with 4 Token.
Whenever a Survivor is hooked onto a Scourge Hook for the first time, Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance consumes -1 Token and applies the following effects:
Causes the Generator with the most progression to explode, damaging it.
Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by 10/15/20 % of its total Progression.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors repairing the Damaged Generator to scream.
This does not trigger a Loud Noise Notification.
Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance is disabled for the remainder of the Trial once all Tokens are consumed.

alts.name: Barbecue & Chilli
alts.desc:
A deep bond with The Entity unlocks potential in one's Aura-reading ability.
After hooking a Survivor, all Survivors who are at least 60/50/40 metres away from that Hook have their Aura revealed to you for 5 seconds.

builds.name: Beginner Perks Only
notes: Only uses perks available to this Killer or global perks available to everyone. It might include some alternative perk ideas from one of the five free Killers too.

perks.name: Undone
perks.desc:
For every time you hook a Survivor, Undone gains +1 Token, up to a maximum of 1/2/3 Token(s).
Performing the Damage Generator action on a Generator consumes all accumulated Tokens and applies the following effects:
Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by a stack-able -10 % of its total Progression per Token, up to a maximum of 10/20/30 %.
Blocks the Damaged Generator for 10 seconds per Token, up to a maximum of 10/20/30 seconds.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing once it becomes unblocked.

alts.name: No Holds Barred
alts.desc:
Each time a Generator is completed, No Holds Barred calls upon The Entity for the following effects:
Blocks the Generator with the most Progression for 15/20/25 seconds.
The Aura of the Blocked Generator is highlighted to you in white.

perks.name: Unforeseen
perks.desc:
After performing the Damage Generator action on a Generator, you benefit from the following effects for 22/26/30 seconds:
Transfers your Terror Radius to the damaged Generator.
This Terror Radius is set to 32 metres.
Grants the Undetectable Status Effect.
Unforeseen has a cool-down of 30 seconds.

alts.name: Hex: Fortune's Fool
alts.desc:
If there is still a Dull Totem in the environment, Hex: Fortune's Fool lights a Hex Totem whenever you hook a Survivor for the first time, cursing them with its Hex Effects.
Inflicts the Oblivious Status Effect.
Blocks the Hex Totem for all other Survivors for 90 seconds.
Blocked Hex Totems cannot be cleansed or blessed by Survivors.
This does not affect the Cursed Survivor.
The Aura of the Hex Totem is revealed to the Cursed Survivor within 24/20/16 metres.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

perks.name: Bitter Murmur
perks.desc:
Unlocks potential in your Aura-reading ability.
Whenever a Generator is completed, Bitter Murmur triggers its primary effect:
The Auras of any Survivors within 20 metres of that Generator are revealed to you for 10 seconds.
Once the last Generator is completed, Bitter Murmur triggers its secondary effect:
The Auras of all Survivors are revealed to you for 16/18/20 seconds.

alts.name: Spies from the Shadows
alts.desc:
Whenever a Survivor startles a Crow within 36/38/40 metres of your location, Spies from the Shadows triggers its effect:
Alerts you with a unique Loud Noise Notification in the shape of a Crow.
Spies from the Shadows has a cool-down of 3 seconds between alerts.

perks.name: Hex: No One Escapes Death
perks.desc:
Once the Exit Gates are powered, if there is still a Dull Totem remaining in the environment, Hex: No One Escapes Death activates and lights it:
Grants a 2/3/4 % Haste Status Effect.
Causes all Survivors to suffer from the Exposed Status Effect.
Once the Status Effect is revealed to Survivors, Hex: No One Escapes Death triggers the following effect:
The Aura of its Hex Totem is revealed to all Survivors within 4 metres.
This range gradually expands to 24 metres over the course of 30 seconds.
Hex: No One Escapes Death remains inactive if no Dull Totems are available.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

alts.name: Sloppy Butcher
alts.desc:
Survivors hit with your vicious Basic Attack suffer from the following effects for 70/80/90 seconds:
Inflicts the Haemorrhage and Mangled Status Effects.
Modifies the potency of Haemorrhage:
Increases the Spawn frequency of Pools of Blood by 50/75/100 %.
Increases the Regression rate of partial Healing progression by +25 %.

alts.name: Unrelenting
alts.desc:
Basic Attacks benefit from the following effect:
Increases the recovery speed of missed basic-attacks by 30/35/40 %.
Increases the recovery speed of successful basic-attacks by 10 %.

addons.name: Captured by the Dark
addons.comment: Automatically weakens all Survivors at the start of the match. This helps in your first chases and also encourages them to seek you out to remove it, which can buy you quite a bit of time. Keep in mind that the add-on has the small downside of reducing the maximum amount of hallucinations that you can place on the map (from 4 to 3).
addons.desc:
Modifies UVX with the following effects:
All Survivors start the Trial in the Weakened State.
Reduces the number of Hallucinations that can exist at the same time by 1.

addons.name: Iridescent OSS Report
addons.comment: After a teleport, the Unknown normally leaves a fake decoy behind. This add-on greatly extends the time it stays up and also gives it a terror radius (which does apply the effects of any relevant perks). Additionally, it also provides a reduction of 5 seconds to the teleport cooldown (which goes from 25 to 20 seconds). Unlike some of the other strong add-ons, this one has no immediate downside and as such it is a very safe choice for anyone to use.
addons.desc:
Modifies UVX with the following effects:
Reduces the Cool-down duration of the Teleport ability by -5 seconds.
Increases the Lifetime of Decoys by +10 seconds.
Causes Decoys to emit a Terror Radius and Red Stain.

addons.name: B-Movie Poster
addons.comment: Applies the Broken status effect to any Survivor you injure for a brief period. Also works when hitting Survivors with Endurance when they go into Deep Wound. The duration isn't very long, but it can still be helpful to prevent a Survivor from immediately using a medkit or getting healed passively by perks such as "Adrenaline".
addons.desc:
Survivors damaged by UVX suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Broken Status Effect for 30 seconds.

addons.name: Hypnotist's Watch
addons.comment: A much simpler way to inflict exhaustion than its purple counterpart. Keep in mind that the projectile has to physically hit the Survivor while it's airborne, not just with the explosion. When your UVX projectile goes through a Survivor it plays a special sound effect that is quite easy to recognize, letting you know that this add-on has been applied.
addons.desc:
Survivors hit by an airborne UVX Projectile suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Exhausted Status Effect for 15 seconds.

addons.name: Obscure Game Cartridge
addons.comment: Increases your action speed for a brief moment after teleporting. It's almost always useful, but keep in mind that the Unknown has tools to play around pallets and windows without having to vault or destroy them, so it's not always extremely impactful in that regard.
addons.desc:
After teleporting to a Hallucination, Obscure Game Cartridge triggers its effect for 20 seconds:
Increases the Action speeds for Breaking, Damaging, and Vaulting by +30 %.

addons.name: Sketch Attempt
addons.comment: Applies the Oblivious status effect briefly after a UVX blast. Not extremely impactful when you focus on one Survivor at a time and chase them in an open area with high visibility, but it can be quite confusing when you blast multiple people at a time or quickly switch targets. The sudden loss of a terror radius can also be very confusing if Survivors lose sight of you and lead into small but meaningful mistakes. Definitely a decent effect for an add-on of this rarity.
addons.desc:
Survivors in the Blast Area of the UVX Projectile suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Oblivious Status Effect for 20 seconds.

addons.name: Footprint Cast
addons.comment: This add-on saves 5 seconds worth of recovery on each UVX hit, not 15 seconds as the description would suggest. The add-on itself is simply boosting the already existing default value of 10 to 15. Not a terrible effect but it's generally outclassed by the blue Front-Page article and other add-ons.
addons.desc:
Whenever a Survivor enters the Weakened State, Footprint Cast triggers its effect:
Reduces the Spawn timer of the next Hallucination by -15 seconds.

addons.name: Front-Page Article
addons.comment: Helps quite a bit, especially in early chases if you break a pallet or wall, to ensure that you're leaving at least one clone behind. One of the better options to improve your hallucination spawn timer if you're planning to use the blue Vanishing Box, which comes with a heavy downside.
addons.desc:
Whenever you break a Breakable Wall or a dropped Pallet, Front-Page Article triggers its effect:
Reduces the Spawn timer of the next Hallucination by -50 %.

addons.name: Notebook of Theories
addons.comment: Provides a small boost to the duration of the Hindered status effect that Survivors get when hit directly by your projectile before it explodes. A small effect, but it doesn't hurt to have it. When your UVX projectile goes through a Survivor it plays a special sound effect that is quite easy to recognize, letting you know that the hinder effect is happening.
addons.desc:
Survivors hit by an airborne UVX Projectile suffer from the following effect:
Increases the duration of the Hindered Status Effect by +2 seconds to 5 seconds.

addons.name: Blurry Photo
addons.comment: On top of slightly reducing the slowdown that occurs after a teleport, it also allows you to hit a Survivor or perform an action sooner. Not a bad effect at all considering its rarity.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Teleport ability with the following effect:
Increases the Recovery rate back to full Movement speed after Teleportation by +7 %.

addons.name: Vanishing Box
addons.comment: Weakens any Survivors that finish repairing a generator. Can also apply to multiple Survivors if they finish the generator together. This is overall a fantastic effect that can punish Survivors that finish a generator in front of you or lead to an easy injury later on. Additionally, Survivors that become weakened by this add-on also speed up your next hallucination spawn (just as if you had weakened them yourself directly). However, this add-on comes with a massive nerf to your hallucination spawn timer which will be very noticeable throughout the game. It's recommended that you try to use another add-on to make up for this, such as the blue Front-Page Article. Overall, this add-on can be a decent crutch when playing against beginner Survivors but you will likely want to stop using it when going against stronger opponents.
addons.desc:
Modifies UVX with the following primary effect:
Increases the default value of the Spawn timer of Hallucinations by +120 %.
Whenever one or multiple Survivors complete a Generator, Vanishing Box triggers its secondary effect:
Causes all participating Survivors to enter the Weakened State.

addons.name: Victim's Map
addons.comment: Briefly reveals the location of Survivors with Killer Instinct when they stare at you long enough to remove their weakened status. Not incredibly useful, but it can occasionally reveal the location of Survivors that you might have not been aware of.
addons.desc:
Survivors performing the Stare Down The Unknown action successfully suffer from the following effect:
Triggers Killer Instinct for 3 seconds.

addons.name: Slashed Backpack
addons.comment: The main utility of this add-on is to help you remove unnecessary Hallucinations from afar and reset them in better spots very quickly. The ability to detonate your UVX projectile on a clone is sometimes useful but definitely won't come into play very often. A nice add-on to pair with the blue Vanishing Box to counter its downside.
addons.desc:
Hitting a Hallucination with the UVX Projectile triggers the following effects:
Causes the Hallucination to disintegrate, creating a Blast Area.
Reduces the Spawn timer of your next Hallucination by -65 %.

addons.name: Device of Undisclosed Origin
addons.comment: Applies a sudden dose of Oblivious status effect to anyone coming close to your hallucinations. This can sometimes backfire and actually warn them that they're running into one, but for the most part this add-on is a simple way to occasionally mess with Survivors and keep them guessing about your actual location. Probably not a good idea to combine this with the green Last Known Recording, since you'd be actively making it less likely to come into play.
addons.desc:
While within range of seeing the Aura of a Hallucination, Survivors suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Oblivious Status Effect.

addons.name: Last Known Recording
addons.comment: Reduces visible aura range of your clones (by default 8m) by almost 3m. Not a huge direct impact outside of chase, but anything that keeps Survivors unaware of your hallucinations is helpful, especially if you teleport to them during chase.
addons.desc:
Modifies Hallucinations with the following effect:
Reduces the range at which Survivors can see their Auras by -35 %.

addons.name: Homemade Mask
addons.comment: Applies a 60 second long Blindness effect to Survivors who dispel your clones. Quite a mediocre effect that doesn't even happen if Survivors ignore your hallucinations, but that is a pretty optimal scenario for you anyway.
addons.desc:
Survivors performing the Dispelling action successfully suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Blindness Status Effect for 60 seconds.

addons.name: Serum Vial
addons.comment: Exhaustion is useful, but it's hard to tell when this add-on has applied its effect since it's only triggered when a Survivor walks into the range of a Hallucination, making it inferior to its blue counterpart.
addons.desc:
Upon entering the range of seeing the Aura of a Hallucination, Survivors suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Exhausted Status Effect for 15 seconds.

addons.name: Punctured Eyeball
addons.comment: Inflicts the Deep Wound status effect on injured Survivors that dispel a hallucination while weakened. The effect itself is quite powerful, but it's too situational to be reliable.
addons.desc:
Survivors performing the Dispelling action successfully while both injured and in the Weakened State suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Deep Wound Status Effect.

addons.name: Rabbit's Foot
addons.comment: Applies the Haemorrhage status effect for an extremely brief period of time after a hit, so short that it's almost useless. Only really helpful if you managed to land a hit on a group of Survivors that were healing, since you could potentially revert their healing progress. Also increases the visibility of pools of blood when charging your power, but this doesn't have much of an impact in regular gameplay since it's not a very good idea to walk around holding the power button because it slows you down significantly. Tapping the power button repeteadly does allow you to move at normal speed, but unfortunately this doesn't help to make the blood consistently brigther.
addons.desc:
While charging UVX, you benefit from the following primary effect:
Pools of Blood are highlighted in bright red.
Survivors damaged by UVX suffer from the following secondary effect:
Inflicts the Haemorrhage Status Effect for 45 seconds.

addons.name: Discarded Milk Carton
addons.comment: The increased bounciness is unnecessary in most scenarios and the unpredictable behaviour of your projectile will likely mess with your muscle memory if you're still learning the basics of this Killer. However, advanced players might opt to run this add-on and play into its unique strengths, namely the fact that your shots are now faster and are sometimes much harder to react against, especially for Survivors who are only used to the Unknown's default projectile speed. Keep in mind that this add-on makes it significantly harder to detonate the UVX blast on a flat floor in front of you, although you can try to compensate this by making it bounce of walls into the ground more often instead. Overall, a very risky add-on that should only be used by veteran players willing to specialize in its use.
addons.desc:
Modifies UVX with the following effects:
Doubles the Bounce strength of the UVX Projectile by changing the following:
Increases Bounciness by +8 %.
Reduces Friction by -15 %.

When you hook the Obsession, the following effects apply to a random Survivor:
Causes the Survivor to scream and reveal their location to the Killer.
They become the new Obsession.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.
perks.name: Friends ‘Til the End

perks.desc: After hooking a Survivor, for 40/50/60 seconds, press the Active Ability button to make a target generator within 20 meters explode, lose -10 % progress, and start regressing.
perks.name: Turn Back The Clock

The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Start the Trial with 4 Token.

Causes the Generator with the most progression to explode, damaging it.
Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by 10/15/20 % of its total Progression.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing afterwards.

This does not trigger a Loud Noise Notification.

perks.desc:
After hooking a Survivor, Pop Goes the Weasel activates for 35/40/45 seconds.
While active, manually damaging a Generator triggers the following effect:
Increases the regression amount by +15 % resulting in 20 % regression.
Pop Goes the Weasel deactivates after use or once its timer elapses.
perks.name: Pop Goes the Weasel

perks.desc:
Your prayers invoke a dark power that meddles with the Survivors' chances of survival.
At the start of the Trial, the 3 Generators located farthest from you are blocked by The Entity for 80/100/120 seconds.
Corrupt Intervention deactivates prematurely once the first Survivor is put into the Dying State.
perks.name: Corrupt Intervention

perks.desc:
Performing the Damage Generator action on Generators highlights their Auras in yellow.
Whenever a Survivor enters the Dying State by any means, Eruption triggers the following effects on all highlighted Generators:
Causes them to explode, damaging them.
Instantly regresses them by -10 % of their total Progression.
Causes them to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors currently repairing them to suffer from the following effects:
Causes them to scream.
Their Auras are revealed to you for 8/10/12 seconds.
Eruption has a cool-down of 30 seconds after triggering its effects, which also resets the highlighted Auras.
perks.name: Eruption

killers.name: The Lich
killers.otzComment:
The Lich possesses four different spells with their own unique cooldown that grant him a variety of abilities including mobility, tracking and tools to help in chase. Using each spell appropriately and managing their downtime is essential to succeed with him.
Vecna is a standard Killer, but the sheer amount of multi-tasking required to use his spells correctly makes him a very difficult pick for beginners. His perks are also mediocre or way too niche for beginners to benefit from.

teachables.name: Dark Arrogance
teachables.desc:
Whenever you are vaulting a Window, you benefit from the following effect:
Increases the Vaulting speed by 15/20/25 %.
Increases all missed basic-attack recovery speeds by 15/20/25 %.
Whenever you are stunned with a Pallet or blinded by any means, you suffer from the following effects:
Reduces the Recovery speed from Pallet Stuns by -25 %.
Increases the duration of Killer Blinds by +25 %.

teachables.name: Languid Touch
teachables.desc:
When a Survivor scares off a Crow within 36 metres of your location, Languid Touch activates:
Causes that Survivor to suffer from the Exhausted Status Effect for 6/8/10 seconds.
Languid Touch has a cool-down of 5 seconds.

teachables.name: Weave Attunement
teachables.desc:
Whenever an Item is depleted for the first time, it is automatically dropped:
The Auras of dropped Survivor Items are revealed to you, as well as the Auras of any Survivors within 12 metres of them.
Affected Survivors see the Aura of that Item as well.
Causes Survivors picking up a Survivor Item to suffer from the Oblivious Status Effect for 20/25/30 seconds.

builds.name: Generic Build
notes: Reliable and well-rounded build. However, it's slightly difficult to modify since it relies on certain perks. Check the suggested alternative perks for some other viable choices.
The first two perks are the foundation; the help with tracking and chase. The final two are focused on gen-related effects.
Using both of the compromised gen perks (Machine Learning & Help Wanted) is ideal for very aggressive players but switching one out for something else is completely fine as well.

perks.name: Barbecue & Chilli
perks.desc:
A deep bond with The Entity unlocks potential in one's Aura-reading ability.
After hooking a Survivor, all Survivors who are at least 60/50/40 metres away from that Hook have their Aura revealed to you for 5 seconds.

alts.name: Lethal Pursuer
alts.desc:
At the start of the Trial, the Auras of all Survivors are revealed to you for 7/8/9 seconds.
Extends the duration of all instances of a Survivor Aura being revealed to you by +2 seconds.
Lethal Pursuer benefits from its own effect.

perks.name: Rapid Brutality
perks.desc:
You move with a speed and fury that makes blood run cold.
You can no longer gain the Bloodlust Status Effect.
Successfully hitting a Survivor with a Basic Attack grants you a +5 % Haste Status Effect for 8/9/10 seconds.

alts.name: Unrelenting
alts.desc:
Basic Attacks benefit from the following effect:
Increases the recovery speed of missed basic-attacks by 30/35/40 %.
Increases the recovery speed of successful basic-attacks by 10 %.

alts.name: Sloppy Butcher
alts.desc:
Survivors hit with your vicious Basic Attack suffer from the following effects for 70/80/90 seconds:
Inflicts the Haemorrhage and Mangled Status Effects.
Modifies the potency of Haemorrhage:
Increases the Spawn frequency of Pools of Blood by 50/75/100 %.
Increases the Regression rate of partial Healing progression by +25 %.

perks.name: Help Wanted
perks.desc:
After performing the Damage Generator action, Help Wanted activates:
Causes that Generator to become a Compromised Generator.
Up to 3 Generators can be Compromised at a time.
The Auras of all Compromised Generators are highlighted to you in yellow.
Once a Compromised Generator is completed, Help Wanted triggers its effects for 70/80/90 seconds:
Increases the Recovery speed of successful Basic Attacks by +25 %.
All Generators not being repaired will automatically regress at 150 % of the default Regression rate.
Additionally, all other Generators are no longer Compromised.

alts.name: Pop Goes the Weasel
alts.desc:
After hooking a Survivor, Pop Goes the Weasel activates for 35/40/45 seconds.
While active, manually damaging a Generator triggers the following effect:
Increases the regression amount by +15 % resulting in 20 % regression.
Pop Goes the Weasel deactivates after use or once its timer elapses.

alts.name: Lay Waste
alts.desc:
Damaging a Generator makes it regress +2 % faster for each Charge it has.
This perk has a cool-down of 55/50/45 seconds after damaging a Generator.

perks.name: Machine Learning
perks.desc:
After performing the Damage Generator action, Machine Learning activates:
Causes that Generator to become a Compromised Generator.
Up to 3 Generators can be Compromised at a time.
The Auras of all Compromised Generators are highlighted to you in yellow.
Once a Compromised Generator is completed, you benefit from the following effects for 40/50/60 seconds:
Undetectable Status Effect
+8 % Haste Status Effect
Additionally, all other Generators are no longer Compromised.

alts.name: Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance
alts.desc:
Overwhelming pain reverberates outwards.
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Start the Trial with 4 Token.
Whenever a Survivor is hooked onto a Scourge Hook for the first time, Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance consumes -1 Token and applies the following effects:
Causes the Generator with the most progression to explode, damaging it.
Instantly regresses the Damaged Generator by 10/15/20 % of its total Progression.
Causes the Damaged Generator to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors repairing the Damaged Generator to scream.
This does not trigger a Loud Noise Notification.
Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance is disabled for the remainder of the Trial once all Tokens are consumed.

perks.name: Hex: Blood Favour
perks.desc:
Hex: Blood Favour lights a Hex Totem at the start of the Trial, cursing Survivors with its Hex Effects.
Whenever a Survivor loses a Health State by a basic-attack, Hex: Blood Favour triggers its effect for 13/14/15 seconds:
Blocks all upright Pallets within 32 metres of that Survivor.
Blocked Pallets cannot be dropped by any Survivor.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

perks.name: Hex: Ruin
perks.desc:
All Generators not currently being repaired experience the following effect:
Causes them to automatically regress at 100/125/150 % of the default Regression rate.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

alts.name: Grim Embrace
alts.desc:
Your act of servitude to The Entity has not gone unnoticed.
Each time a Survivor is hooked for the first time, Grim Embrace gains +1 Token and activates once you are at least 16 metres away from the Hook:
1-3 Tokens: Blocks all Generators for 6/8/10 seconds.
4 Tokens: Blocks all Generators for 40 seconds and the Aura of the Obsession is revealed to you for 6 seconds.

perks.name: Hex: Undying
perks.desc:
Whenever a Survivor is within 2/3/4 metres of a Dull Totem, Hex: Undying triggers its primary effect:
Their Aura is revealed to you for as long as they remain in that range.
Whenever a Hex Totem is cleansed, Hex: Undying triggers its secondary effect:
Transfers the cleansed Hex to the Hex Totem associated with Hex: Undying instead, replacing it.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

alts.name: No Holds Barred
alts.desc:
Each time a Generator is completed, No Holds Barred calls upon The Entity for the following effects:
Blocks the Generator with the most Progression for 15/20/25 seconds.
The Aura of the Blocked Generator is highlighted to you in white.

perks.name: Friends 'til the End
perks.desc:
When you hook any Survivors that is not the Obsession, the following effects apply to the Obsession:
Their Aura is revealed for 6/8/10 seconds.
They suffer from the Exposed Status Effect for 20 seconds.
When you hook the Obsession, the following effects apply to a random Survivor:
Causes the Survivor to scream and reveal their location to the Killer.
They become the new Obsession.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.

perks.name: Furtive Chase
perks.desc:
After hooking the Obsession, you benefit from the following effects for 14/16/18 seconds:
Grants the Undetectable Status Effect.
Grants a +10 % Haste Status Effect.
Whenever the Obsession is unhooked by another Survivor, the Obsession Status transfers to their Rescuer.
You can only be obsessed with one Survivor at a time.

perks.name: Surge
perks.desc:
Whenever you put a Survivor into the Dying State with your Basic Attack, Surge triggers its effect:
Causes all Generators within 32 metres of your location to instantly explode and start regressing.
Instantly regresses all affected Generators by 6/7/8 %.

perks.name: Hex: No One Escapes Death
perks.desc:
Once the Exit Gates are powered, if there is still a Dull Totem remaining in the environment, Hex: No One Escapes Death activates and lights it:
Grants a 2/3/4 % Haste Status Effect.
Causes all Survivors to suffer from the Exposed Status Effect.
Once the Status Effect is revealed to Survivors, Hex: No One Escapes Death triggers the following effect:
The Aura of its Hex Totem is revealed to all Survivors within 4 metres.
This range gradually expands to 24 metres over the course of 30 seconds.
Hex: No One Escapes Death remains inactive if no Dull Totems are available.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

alts.name: Coup de Grâce
alts.desc:
As the end nears, you go in for the kill.
Whenever a Generator is completed, Coup de Grâce gains +2 Tokens, up to a maximum of 10 Tokens per Trial:
Increases the range of your next Lunge Attack by 70/75/80 %, while consuming -1 Token.
Coup de Grâce can only hold a maximum of 5 Tokens at a time.

alts.name: Rapid Brutality
alts.desc:
You move with a speed and fury that makes blood run cold.
You can no longer gain the Bloodlust Status Effect.
Successfully hitting a Survivor with a Basic Attack grants you a +5 % Haste Status Effect for 8/9/10 seconds.

builds.name: Beginner Perks Only
notes: Only uses perks available to this Killer or global perks available to everyone. It might include some alternative perk ideas from one of the five free Killers too.
Unrelenting is a very simple perk that helps you recover faster after each attack. You can also try Deerstalker or another information perk if you're struggling to find Survivors.

Deerstalker will reveal you and a Survivor to each other periodically. It will also make all special items that show your aura backfire on the user and reveal their aura to you when using certain spells!

perks.name: No Holds Barred
perks.desc:
Each time a Generator is completed, No Holds Barred calls upon The Entity for the following effects:
Blocks the Generator with the most Progression for 15/20/25 seconds.
The Aura of the Blocked Generator is highlighted to you in white.

perks.desc:

Modifies the potency of Haemorrhage:
Increases the Spawn frequency of Pools of Blood by 50/75/100 %.
Increases the Regression rate of partial Healing progression by +25 %.

alts.name: Scourge Hook: Weeping Wounds
alts.desc:
At the start of the Trial, 4 Hooks in the environment are changed into Scourge Hooks:
The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.
Each time a Survivor is unhooked from a Scourge Hook, the following effects apply:
Causes that Survivor to suffer from the Haemorrhage Status Effect for 90 seconds.
After the first time that Survivor is healed back to full health, they suffer from the following effect until they are injured again by any means:
Reduces their Action speeds for Healing and Repairing by 10/13/16 %.

perks.name: Unrelenting
perks.desc:
Basic Attacks benefit from the following effect:
Increases the recovery speed of missed basic-attacks by 30/35/40 %.
Increases the recovery speed of successful basic-attacks by 10 %.

alts.name: Deerstalker
alts.desc:
Unlocks potential in your Aura-reading ability.
Whenever a Survivor reads your Aura, Deerstalker activates for the same duration as their Aura-reading action:
The Aura of that Survivor is revealed to you.
Furthermore, the following effect triggers automatically every 40/35/30 seconds:
Your Aura is revealed for 4 seconds to the Survivor with currently the lowest cumulative Chase time.

alts.name: Spies from the Shadows
alts.desc:
Whenever a Survivor startles a Crow within 36/38/40 metres of your location, Spies from the Shadows triggers its effect:
Alerts you with a unique Loud Noise Notification in the shape of a Crow.
Spies from the Shadows has a cool-down of 3 seconds between alerts.

alts.name: Whispers
alts.desc:
Whenever any Survivor is within 28/26/24 metres of your location:
Causes you to hear the sporadic whispers of The Entity, indicating a Survivor's presence.
Whenever any Survivor is outside 28/26/24 metres of your location:
Gain +5 % Haste Status Effect.

perks.name: Hex: No One Escapes Death
perks.desc:
Once the Exit Gates are powered, if there is still a Dull Totem remaining in the environment, Hex: No One Escapes Death activates and lights it:
Grants a 2/3/4 % Haste Status Effect.
Causes all Survivors to suffer from the Exposed Status Effect.
Once the Status Effect is revealed to Survivors, Hex: No One Escapes Death triggers the following effect:
The Aura of its Hex Totem is revealed to all Survivors within 4 metres.
This range gradually expands to 24 metres over the course of 30 seconds.
Hex: No One Escapes Death remains inactive if no Dull Totems are available.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

alts.name: Hex: Fortune's Fool
alts.desc:
If there is still a Dull Totem in the environment, Hex: Fortune's Fool lights a Hex Totem whenever you hook a Survivor for the first time, cursing them with its Hex Effects.
Inflicts the Oblivious Status Effect.
Blocks the Hex Totem for all other Survivors for 90 seconds.
Blocked Hex Totems cannot be cleansed or blessed by Survivors.
This does not affect the Cursed Survivor.
The Aura of the Hex Totem is revealed to the Cursed Survivor within 24/20/16 metres.
The Hex Effects persist until the Hex Totem is either blessed or cleansed by a Survivor, disabling it for the remainder of the Trial.

addons.name: Iridescent Book of Vile Darkness
addons.comment: Reduces the amount of skulls in your projectile attack, but also lowers it to ground level to make it impossible to dodge by crouching. Also makes your flight capable of blocking windows for an extended period of time if you fly over them, which is particularly helpful in structures like shack or certain main buildings. Despite the initial downside, this add-on brings a lot of utility and holds great value for anyone who wants to specialize in learning how to play with it. Keep in mind that you can increase the skulls from 2 to 3 if you pair with the blue Ornate Horn add-on. While powerful, this add-on fundamentally changes how Vecna's power works and it might be a bad idea to get used to it while you learn this Killer, as you may grow  dependent on it.
addons.desc:
Whenever you use the Fly Spell to pass through a Window, the following effects apply:
Blocks the Window for all Survivors for 45 seconds.
Modifies the Flight of the Damned Spell with the following effects:
Reduces the Flight height of the Flying Entites by -0.7 metres, allowing them to also damage Survivors who are crouching.
Reduces the number of Flying Entities summoned by the Spell by 3.

addons.name: Bag of Holding
addons.comment: This add-on guarantees that two out of the six magical chests will be mimics, slowing down Survivors and reducing their chances to obtain useful magical items early on. Since those mimics remain, it also forces Survivors to share other chests and wait for the long cooldown before new magical items respawn. Clumsy Survivors might even take damage if they fail the mimic skill check interaction. It also makes them Oblivious briefly after using these chests. Overall, a decent effect if you want to run an add-on that doesn't require you to plan around it.
addons.desc:
Survivors opening a Treasure Chest suffer from the following effects:
Inflicts the Oblivious Status Effect for 15 seconds.
At least 2 Treasure Chests in the environment will roll a 1 on their Dice Roll.

addons.name: Robe of Eyes
addons.comment: Occasionally reveals the auras of Survivors anywhere on the map if they happen to be near one of the six magical item chests when you use a spell. Since using spells often is already a good idea in general, the effects of this add-on will often trigger throughout the match, giving you information about Survivors both near and far. Pairs particularly well with the perk Lethal Pursuer which will extend the duration of each aura read by two seconds. If you use this add-on, consider pairing it with other add-ons that allow you to cycle through spells more quickly such as the blue Pearl of Power. Sometimes, it might be worth to even use a spell randomly just for the chance to find a Survivor with it.
addons.desc:
Whenever you cast any Spell, all Survivors within 6 metres of a Treasure Chest suffer from the following effect:
Their Auras are revealed to you for 4 seconds.

addons.name: Raven's Feather
addons.comment: Slightly increases the time that you can fly by an extra 0.5 seconds, which overall gives you about ~4 extra meters of distance by the end of your flight. A really useful effect (especially considering its rarity) if you plan on using your Fly spell for maximum mobility. Keep in mind, however, that many times you don't even need to use the full length of the flight anyway.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Fly Spell with the following effect:
Extends the Flight duration by +0.5 seconds.

addons.name: Pearl of Power
addons.comment: Reduces your spell cooldowns by 2 seconds whenever you land a basic attack. More situational than the green Ring of Spell Storing, but still very useful since it can almost guarantee that you'll be able to use your spells sooner in prolonged encounters or right after a down, even though your normal spell cooldown is already pretty short. It's a safe add-on to use if you're looking for a simple but dependable effect.
addons.desc:
Successfully hitting a Survivor with a Basic Attack triggers the following effect:
Reduces the remaining Recharge time of all Spells currently on cool-down by -2 seconds.

addons.name: Ornate Horn
addons.comment: Spawns an extra skull for your projectile attack, making it slightly harder for Survivors to find a gap between them to dodge it. Keep in mind that they can still be dodged by crouching. Particularly useful when paired with the Iridescent Book of Vile Darkness, since it gives you 3 skulls in total. Having 3 skulls makes aiming easier, since one of them will face exactly in front of you at all times.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Flight of the Damned Spell with the following effect:
Increases the number of Flying Entities summoned by the Spell by 1.

addons.name: Staff of Withering
addons.comment: Inflicts Exhaustion on any survivor detected by the Dispelling Sphere. Can be used preemptively as you approach a Survivor or aggressively during chase if you want to deny a Survivor from using their exhaustion perk. However, not every Survivor runs exhaustion perks so the effect of this add-on can be highly situational.
addons.desc:
Whenever a Survivor enters radius of the Dispelling Sphere, they suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Exhausted Status Effect for 30 seconds.

addons.name: Ring of Spell Storing
addons.comment: Consistently reduces the cooldown of all spells by a small margin of 1 second. This effect is universally useful since it applies to all cooldowns throughout the game but a single second is often not that big of a deal. Definitely a decent add-on for its rarity.
addons.desc:
You benefit from the following effect:
Reduces the default Recharge time of all Spells by -1 second.

addons.name: Lantern of Revealing
addons.comment: A very simple and useful add-on that reveals the auras of Survivors that narrowly dodge your projectile attack. On top of being a solid effect that will trigger often, it also allows you to understand why exactly your attack missed so that you can be more accurate the next time. It benefits from being used together with the perk Lethal Pursuer since it will extend the aura duration by 2 seconds.
addons.desc:
Survivors narrowly missed by the Flying Entities summoned by the Flight of the Damned Spell suffer from the following effect:
Their Auras are revealed to you for 3 seconds.

addons.name: Dragontooth Dagger
addons.comment: Inflicts Mangled and Haemorrhage to any Survivor hit by a basic attack if they have a magical item. Can be triggered quite consistently, but its duration is limited to 60 seconds which sometimes hinders its potential. Does not pair well with the purple Bag of Holding, since ideally you want Survivors to actually hold magical items to trigger this add-on's effect. Some Survivors don't even bother to pick up magical items throughout the match, and sadly this add-on will never trigger any effect on them.
addons.desc:
Successfully hitting a Survivor equipped with a Magic Item with a Basic Attack triggers the following effect:
Inflicts the Haemorrhage and Mangled Status Effects for 60 seconds.

addons.name: Cloak of Invisibility
addons.comment: Gives you 20 seconds of Undetectable anytime all of your spells are on cooldown. It's not very easy to have this occur naturally, since the cooldowns of some spells are quite short, but you can always go out of your way to force it so you can benefit from this effect.
addons.desc:
Whenever all four Spells are on cool-down at the same time, you benefit from the following effect:
Grants the Undetectable Status Effect for 20 seconds.

addons.name: Glass Eye
addons.comment: Increases the size and speed of the Dispelling Sphere, making it slightly more effective at covering big distances or hitting someone right in front of you before they can dodge it. Not a terrible effect and pretty helpful when you're using other add-ons that trigger only with the Dispelling Sphere, such as the Staff of Withering.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Dispelling Sphere Spell with the following effects:
Increases the its radius by +2 metres.
Increases its Travel speed by +10 %.

addons.name: Boots of Speed
addons.comment: Provides a very small dose of Haste, increasing your movement speed briefly after using the Mage Hand spell. Not necessary in every situation, and even in the best case scenario, the effect itself is incredibly small. Considering its rarity, you're probably better off with something else.
addons.desc:
After casting the Mage Hand Spell, you benefit from the following effect:
Grants a +3 % Haste Status Effect for 2 seconds.

addons.name: Crystal Ball
addons.comment: Being able to track the Survivors hit by the Dispelling Sphere a bit longer is not a terrible effect, especially if you are dilligent at using it as often as possible. It doesn't help a lot when detecting Survivors from afar, but it can make the difference when tracking a Survivor with unpredictable movement who has managed to slip out of your sight.
addons.desc:
Whenever the Dispelling Sphere Spell detects a Survivor, you benefit from the following effect:
Increases the duration of Killer Instinct by +1 second.

addons.name: Trickster's Glove
addons.comment: With this add-on, the Mage Hand prevents a pallet from being dropped for an extra 0.3 seconds. This can sometimes give you a bit more margin for error in chase and in some lucky scenarios, it could possibly make it harder for Survivors to rescue a teammate if you pick them up under a pallet that is being held by the Mage Hand. If the Survivor that you pick up is at the center of the pallet, however, even this add-on is not enough to prevent a well-timed pallet rescue. So even for this purpose, this add-on is not 100% consistent either. That being said, if you run the perks Fire Up or Forever Entwined (both of which increase your pick up speed), this add-on can basically guarantee that pallet saves become impossible.
addons.desc:
While casting the Mage Hand Spell to block an upright Pallet, you benefit from the following effect:
Increases its Hold time by +0.3 seconds.

addons.name: Cloak of Elvenkind
addons.comment: Reduces your terror radius by a very large amount (22 meters) during flight. Despite the significant number, the effect itself is massively mitigated by the fact that flying is quite loud already (including a directional sound queue when in close proximity) and Survivors might even be able to see your aura during your flight anyway thanks to a certain magical item from the magical chests. Still, if you use the Fly spell often enough, the large shift in terror radius size will likely confuse Survivors at least a few times per match.
addons.desc:
While casting the Fly Spell, you benefit from the following effect:
Reduces your Terror Radius by -22 metres.
This effect lingers for 6 seconds after ending Fly.

addons.name: Potion of Speed
addons.comment: Reduces the cooldown that occurs after flight, making it slightly easier to hit a Survivor shortly after flying and also slightly increasing your mobility since you spend less time slowed down. That being said, the effect itself is incredibly small and really hard to notice. The brown Raven's Feather is the superior choice if you're looking for an add-on to improve your Fly spell.
addons.desc:
While casting the Fly Spell, you benefit from the following effect:
Reduces the Interaction Cool-down time after casting it by -0.15 seconds.

addons.name: Tattered Headband
addons.comment: The extra range on the damaging skulls is almost never relevant since it's typically used as a close-range attack. Creative players might find ways to take advantage of the extra range, however, especially when paired with the Iridescent Book of Vile Darkness which brings your skeletons closer to ground level. For most players, however, this add-on will rarely make any difference.
addons.desc:
Modifies the Flight of the Damned Spell with the following effect:
Extends the Flight range of the Flying Entities summoned by the Spell by +4 metres.

addons.name: Ring of Telekinesis
addons.comment: Increases your vault speed slightly after blocking a pallet with Mage Hand. This effect is quite small and rather situational, so you might prefer to run an add-on that provides more consistent value. The blue Boots of Speed is probably a better alternative in almost every scenario.
addons.desc:
While casting the Mage Hand Spell to block an upright Pallet, you benefit from the following effect:
Increases your Vaulting speed by +10 % for the next 10 seconds.

addons.name: Vorpal Sword
addons.comment: Gives some anti-healing properties to the Dispelling Sphere and makes the Mage Hand turn into a delayed pallet-breaker instead of the normal instant pallet-lifter. Since the Mage Hand takes a while to break a pallet, it can also be used as a method to block it and prevent a Survivor from vaulting during chase. Overall, this is a questionable tradeoff and not much of an upgrade at all. The default pallet lifting is simply better in most situations. The add-on also gives extra utility to the Dispelling Sphere, but not enough to make it really worth it. If you create a build around this add-on, you can actually make the forced Broken status effect quite a nuisance for Survivors. Otherwise, you probably won't want to use it on its own.
addons.desc:
Whenever an injured Survivor enters radius of the Dispelling Sphere, they suffer from the following effect:
Inflicts the Broken Status Effect for 30 seconds.
Modifies the Mage Hand Spell with the following effect:
Causes it to break dropped Pallets, instead of lifting them.
This action takes 4 seconds to complete.

perks.desc:
After hooking a Survivor, Pop Goes the Weasel activates for 35/40/45 seconds.

Increases the regression amount by +15 % resulting in 20 % regression.
Pop Goes the Weasel deactivates after use or once its timer elapses.
perks.name: Pop Goes the Weasel

perks.desc:
Your prayers invoke a dark power that meddles with the Survivors' chances of survival.
At the start of the Trial, the 3 Generators located farthest from you are blocked by The Entity for 80/100/120 seconds.
Corrupt Intervention deactivates prematurely once the first Survivor is put into the Dying State.

perks.desc:
Performing the Damage Generator action on Generators highlights their Auras in yellow.

Causes them to explode, damaging them.
Instantly regresses them by -10 % of their total Progression.
Causes them to start regressing afterwards.
Causes all Survivors currently repairing them to suffer from the following effects:
Causes them to scream.
Their Auras are revealed to you for 8/10/12 seconds.
Eruption has a cool-down of 30 seconds after triggering its effects, which also resets the highlighted Auras.
perks.name: Eruption

perks.desc:
Overwhelming pain reverberates outwards.

The Auras of these Scourge Hooks are highlighted in white.

Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance is disabled for the remainder of the Trial once all Tokens are consumed.

killers.name: The Dark Lord
killers.otzComment:
The Dark Lord can shapeshift between three different forms that grant him several abilities, each having their own strengths, weaknesses and cooldowns. Mastering the use of each form and switching between them at the right times is key to succeed with him.
Despite having some of the stats of a standard Killer, Dracula is still a very complex character that beginner players might find difficult to fully understand, especially considering that he is a licensed character that must be purchased. His hex-related perks are worth unlocking, however. Wretched Fate is a solid slowdown perk (unless you focus on the Obsession) and Dominance is possibly the best perk in the game to defend hex totems.

teachables.name: Dominance
teachables.desc:
The power you wield over the land strikes terror in the hearts of all who cross your path.
The first time each Totem are interacted with by a Survivor, Dominance triggers its effect:
Calls upon The Entity to block it for 25 seconds.
The Aura of the blocked Prop is revealed to you in white.
The Survivor screams.
The Survivor's aura is revealed to you for 3/4/5 seconds.

teachables.desc:

Reduces their Repair speed by 27/30/33 %.
The Aura of the Hex Totem is revealed to them within 12 metres.

teachables.desc:
One can always rely on the avarice of the living and use it to one's advantage.

The Auras of Survivors coming within 8 metres of unopened or closed Chests are revealed to you for 3/4/5 seconds.
Human Greed has a cool-down of 10 seconds on the ability to kick Chests.

Blocks both Exit Gate Switches for 12 seconds.
This time is extended by an additional 6/9/12 seconds per accumulated Token, up to a combined maximum of 36/48/60 seconds.

builds.name: Simple Flow Build
notes: A super simple build that has several perks that work automatically and don't require a lot of input from you!
Survivors cannot drop a pallet and leave its vicinity without getting hindered by "Knock Out".  You can pressure them in Wolf or Vampire form and sometimes get an easy down.
Your second and third perk provide a bit of information and passive slowdown.

If you don't mind being a bit active, Ultimate Weapon is a great fourth perk to occasionally find Survivors. Otherwise, Spies from the Shadows or any other alternative 4th perk is a good choice that requires little work from you.
